  "TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Simulation.lean": {
    "Turing.Action.apply_workTapes": "lemma Action.apply_workTapes {k : \u2115} {Symbol State : Type*} {input : List Symbol} (a : Action k Symbol State) (c : Cfg k Symbol State input) (i : Fin k) : (a.apply c).workTapes i = Function.update (c.workTapes i) (c.workTapePos i) ((a.workTapes i).1.getD (c.workTapeSymbols i))",
    "Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.spaceUsed_le": "theorem ComputesInTime.spaceUsed_le {M : FinTM Bool} {x y : List Bool} {T : \u2115} (h : M.ComputesInTime x y T) (t : \u2115) : M.tm.spaceUsed (M.tm.initCfg x) t \u2264 M.k * (T + 1)",
    "Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag": "def VirtualTag {n : \u2115} (p : Fin (n + 2)) (b : Bool) : Prop",
    "Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag_iff": "theorem VirtualTag_iff {n : \u2115} (p : Fin (n + 2)) (b : Bool) : VirtualTag p b \u2194 (p.val = 0 \u2192 b = false) \u2227 (p.val = n + 1 \u2192 b = true)",
    "Turing.FinTM.branchTM": "def branchTM (M\u2081 M\u2082 : FinTM Bool) (b : Bool) : FinTM Bool",
    "Turing.FinTM.branchTM_computes": "lemma branchTM_computes (M\u2081 M\u2082 : FinTM Bool) (b : Bool) (x w : List Bool) (t : \u2115) : (branchTM M\u2081 M\u2082 b).ComputesInTime x w t \u2194 (cond b M\u2081 M\u2082).ComputesInTime x w t",
    "Turing.FinTM.branchTM_spaceUsed": "theorem branchTM_spaceUsed (M\u2081 M\u2082 : FinTM Bool) (b : Bool) (x : List Bool) (t : \u2115) : (branchTM M\u2081 M\u2082 b).tm.spaceUsed ((branchTM M\u2081 M\u2082 b).tm.initCfg x) t = if b then M\u2081.tm.spaceUsed (M\u2081.tm.initCfg x) t + M\u2082.k else M\u2082.tm.spaceUsed (M\u2082.tm.initCfg x) t + M\u2081.k",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferTape": "def bufferTape {Symbol : Type*} (w : List Symbol) (z : \u2124) : Option Symbol",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_append": "lemma bufferTape_append {Symbol : Type*} (w : List Symbol) (b : Symbol) : bufferTape (w ++ [b]) = Function.update (bufferTape w) (w.length : \u2124) (some b)",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_eq": "theorem bufferTape_eq {Symbol : Type*} (w : List Symbol) (z : \u2124) : bufferTape w z = if 0 \u2264 z then w[z.toNat]? else none",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_inputSymbol": "lemma bufferTape_inputSymbol {k : \u2115} {S : Type} {w : List Bool} (c : Cfg k Bool S w) : bufferTape w ((c.inputPos.val : \u2124) - 1) = c.inputSymbol",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_left": "@[simp] lemma bufferTape_left {Symbol : Type*} (w : List Symbol) : bufferTape w (-1) = none",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat": "@[simp] lemma bufferTape_nat {Symbol : Type*} (w : List Symbol) (i : \u2115) : bufferTape w i = w[i]?",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nil": "@[simp] lemma bufferTape_nil {Symbol : Type*} : bufferTape (Symbol := Symbol) [] = fun _ => none",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_of_neg": "theorem bufferTape_of_neg {Symbol : Type*} (w : List Symbol) {z : \u2124} (hz : z < 0) : bufferTape w z = none",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM": "def bufferedCompTM (M\u2081 M\u2082 : FinTM Bool) : FinTM Bool",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferedComp_start": "lemma bufferedComp_start (M\u2081 M\u2082 : FinTM Bool) (x y : List Bool) (t\u2081 : \u2115) (h\u2081 : M\u2081.ComputesInTime x y t\u2081) : \u2203 (a : \u2115) (p : Fin (x.length + 2)) (tapes : Fin M\u2081.k \u2192 \u2124 \u2192 Option Bool) (heads : Fin M\u2081.k \u2192 \u2124), a \u2264 t\u2081 + y.length + 2 \u2227 (bufferedCompTM M\u2081 M\u2082).tm.runFrom ((bufferedCompTM M\u2081 M\u2082).tm.initCfg x) a = bufferedSecondCfg M\u2081 M\u2082 (M\u2082.tm.initCfg y) true p tapes heads",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferedFirstCfg": "def bufferedFirstCfg (M\u2081 M\u2082 : FinTM Bool) {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg M\u2081.k Bool M\u2081.State x) : Cfg (bufferedCompTM M\u2081 M\u2082).k Bool (bufferedCompTM M\u2081 M\u2082).State x",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferedFirstCfg_init": "lemma bufferedFirstCfg_init (M\u2081 M\u2082 : FinTM Bool) (x : List Bool) : (bufferedCompTM M\u2081 M\u2082).tm.initCfg x = bufferedFirstCfg M\u2081 M\u2082 (M\u2081.tm.initCfg x)",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferedFirstCfg_rewind": "lemma bufferedFirstCfg_rewind (M\u2081 M\u2082 : FinTM Bool) {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg M\u2081.k Bool M\u2081.State x) (hs : c.state = none) : (bufferedCompTM M\u2081 M\u2082).tm.runFrom (bufferedFirstCfg M\u2081 M\u2082 c) (c.output.length + 2) = bufferedSecondCfg M\u2081 M\u2082 (M\u2082.tm.initCfg c.output) true c.inputPos c.workTapes c.workTapePos",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferedFirstCfg_run": "lemma bufferedFirstCfg_run (M\u2081 M\u2082 : FinTM Bool) {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg M\u2081.k Bool M\u2081.State x) (t : \u2115) (h : \u2200 s, s < t \u2192 (M\u2081.tm.runFrom c s).state \u2260 none) : (bufferedCompTM M\u2081 M\u2082).tm.runFrom (bufferedFirstCfg M\u2081 M\u2082 c) t = bufferedFirstCfg M\u2081 M\u2082 (M\u2081.tm.runFrom c t)",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferedFirstCfg_step": "lemma bufferedFirstCfg_step (M\u2081 M\u2082 : FinTM Bool) {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg M\u2081.k Bool M\u2081.State x) (hs : c.state \u2260 none) : (bufferedCompTM M\u2081 M\u2082).tm.step (bufferedFirstCfg M\u2081 M\u2082 c) = bufferedFirstCfg M\u2081 M\u2082 (M\u2081.tm.step c)",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferedScanCfg": "def bufferedScanCfg (M\u2081 M\u2082 : FinTM Bool) {x : List Bool} (y : List Bool) (p : Fin (x.length + 2)) (tapes : Fin M\u2081.k \u2192 \u2124 \u2192 Option Bool) (heads : Fin M\u2081.k \u2192 \u2124) (j : \u2115) : Cfg (bufferedCompTM M\u2081 M\u2082).k Bool (bufferedCompTM M\u2081 M\u2082).State x",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferedScanCfg_run": "lemma bufferedScanCfg_run (M\u2081 M\u2082 : FinTM Bool) {x : List Bool} (y : List Bool) (p : Fin (x.length + 2)) (tapes : Fin M\u2081.k \u2192 \u2124 \u2192 Option Bool) (heads : Fin M\u2081.k \u2192 \u2124) : \u2200 j, j \u2264 y.length \u2192 (bufferedCompTM M\u2081 M\u2082).tm.runFrom (bufferedScanCfg M\u2081 M\u2082 y p tapes heads j) (j + 1) = bufferedSecondCfg M\u2081 M\u2082 (M\u2082.tm.initCfg y) true p tapes heads",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferedSecondCfg": "def bufferedSecondCfg (M\u2081 M\u2082 : FinTM Bool) {x y : List Bool} (c : Cfg M\u2082.k Bool M\u2082.State y) (b : Bool) (p : Fin (x.length + 2)) (tapes : Fin M\u2081.k \u2192 \u2124 \u2192 Option Bool) (heads : Fin M\u2081.k \u2192 \u2124) : Cfg (bufferedCompTM M\u2081 M\u2082).k Bool (bufferedCompTM M\u2081 M\u2082).State x",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferedSecondCfg_run": "lemma bufferedSecondCfg_run (M\u2081 M\u2082 : FinTM Bool) {x y : List Bool} (c : Cfg M\u2082.k Bool M\u2082.State y) (b : Bool) (hb : VirtualTag c.inputPos b) (p : Fin (x.length + 2)) (tapes : Fin M\u2081.k \u2192 \u2124 \u2192 Option Bool) (heads : Fin M\u2081.k \u2192 \u2124) (t : \u2115) : \u2203 b', VirtualTag (M\u2082.tm.runFrom c t).inputPos b' \u2227 (bufferedCompTM M\u2081 M\u2082).tm.runFrom (bufferedSecondCfg M\u2081 M\u2082 c b p tapes heads) t = bufferedSecondCfg M\u2081 M\u2082 (M\u2082.tm.runFrom c t) b' p tapes heads",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferedSecondCfg_step": "lemma bufferedSecondCfg_step (M\u2081 M\u2082 : FinTM Bool) {x y : List Bool} (c : Cfg M\u2082.k Bool M\u2082.State y) (b : Bool) (hb : VirtualTag c.inputPos b) (p : Fin (x.length + 2)) (tapes : Fin M\u2081.k \u2192 \u2124 \u2192 Option Bool) (heads : Fin M\u2081.k \u2192 \u2124) : \u2203 b', VirtualTag (M\u2082.tm.step c).inputPos b' \u2227 (bufferedCompTM M\u2081 M\u2082).tm.step (bufferedSecondCfg M\u2081 M\u2082 c b p tapes heads) = bufferedSecondCfg M\u2081 M\u2082 (M\u2082.tm.step c) b' p tapes heads",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferedSecondCfg_workTapePos_cast": "theorem bufferedSecondCfg_workTapePos_cast (M\u2081 M\u2082 : FinTM Bool) {x y : List Bool} (c : Cfg M\u2082.k Bool M\u2082.State y) (b : Bool) (p : Fin (x.length + 2)) (tapes : Fin M\u2081.k \u2192 \u2124 \u2192 Option Bool) (heads : Fin M\u2081.k \u2192 \u2124) (i : Fin (bufferedCompTM M\u2081 M\u2082).k) : (bufferedSecondCfg M\u2081 M\u2082 c b p tapes heads).workTapePos i = tapeBlocks heads ((c.inputPos.val : \u2124) - 1) c.workTapePos (Fin.cast (bufferedCompTM_k M\u2081 M\u2082) i)",
    "Turing.FinTM.bufferedSecondCfg_workTapes_cast": "theorem bufferedSecondCfg_workTapes_cast (M\u2081 M\u2082 : FinTM Bool) {x y : List Bool} (c : Cfg M\u2082.k Bool M\u2082.State y) (b : Bool) (p : Fin (x.length + 2)) (tapes : Fin M\u2081.k \u2192 \u2124 \u2192 Option Bool) (heads : Fin M\u2081.k \u2192 \u2124) (i : Fin (bufferedCompTM M\u2081 M\u2082).k) : (bufferedSecondCfg M\u2081 M\u2082 c b p tapes heads).workTapes i = tapeBlocks tapes (bufferTape y) c.workTapes (Fin.cast (bufferedCompTM_k M\u2081 M\u2082) i)",
    "Turing.FinTM.controlAction": "def controlAction {k : \u2115} {S : Type} (m : SignType) (q : Option S) : Action k Bool S",
    "Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply": "lemma controlAction_apply {k : \u2115} {S : Type} {x : List Bool} (cfg : Cfg k Bool S x) (m : SignType) (q : Option S) : (controlAction m q).apply cfg = {cfg with state := q, inputPos := moveInputPos cfg.inputPos m}",
    "Turing.FinTM.emitAction": "def emitAction {k : \u2115} {S : Type} (w : List Bool) (e : Fin (w.length + 1) \u2192 S) (i : Fin (w.length + 1)) : Action k Bool S",
    "Turing.FinTM.emit_halts": "lemma emit_halts {k : \u2115} {S : Type} {x : List Bool} (tm : MultiTapeTM k Bool S) (w : List Bool) (e : Fin (w.length + 1) \u2192 S) (htr : \u2200 i inp work, tm.tr (e i) inp work = emitAction w e i) (cfg : Cfg k Bool S x) (hs : cfg.state = some (e 0)) : (tm.runFrom cfg (w.length + 1)).state = none \u2227 (tm.runFrom cfg (w.length + 1)).output = cfg.output ++ w",
    "Turing.FinTM.emit_run": "lemma emit_run {k : \u2115} {S : Type} {x : List Bool} (tm : MultiTapeTM k Bool S) (w : List Bool) (e : Fin (w.length + 1) \u2192 S) (htr : \u2200 i inp work, tm.tr (e i) inp work = emitAction w e i) (cfg : Cfg k Bool S x) (hs : cfg.state = some (e 0)) : \u2200 t (ht : t \u2264 w.length), (tm.runFrom cfg t).state = some (e \u27e8t, by omega\u27e9) \u2227 (tm.runFrom cfg t).output = cfg.output ++ w.take t",
    "Turing.FinTM.inputSymbol_at": "lemma inputSymbol_at {k : \u2115} {S : Type} {x : List Bool} (cfg : Cfg k Bool S x) (i : \u2115) (hi : i \u2264 x.length) (hp : cfg.inputPos.val = i + 1) : cfg.inputSymbol = x[i]?",
    "Turing.FinTM.leftAction": "def leftAction {k : \u2115} {S S' : Type} (l : \u2115) (f : S \u2192 S') (a : Action k Bool S) : Action (k + l) Bool S'",
    "Turing.FinTM.leftCfg": "def leftCfg {k l : \u2115} {S S' : Type} {x : List Bool} (f : S \u2192 S') (c : Cfg k Bool S x) (tapes : Fin l \u2192 \u2124 \u2192 Option Bool) (heads : Fin l \u2192 \u2124) : Cfg (k + l) Bool S' x",
    "Turing.FinTM.leftCfg_apply": "lemma leftCfg_apply {k l : \u2115} {S S' : Type} {x : List Bool} (f : S \u2192 S') (a : Action k Bool S) (c : Cfg k Bool S x) (tapes : Fin l \u2192 \u2124 \u2192 Option Bool) (heads : Fin l \u2192 \u2124) : (leftAction l f a).apply (leftCfg f c tapes heads) = leftCfg f (a.apply c) tapes heads",
    "Turing.FinTM.leftCfg_run": "lemma leftCfg_run {k l : \u2115} {S S' : Type} {x : List Bool} (tm : MultiTapeTM k Bool S) (tm' : MultiTapeTM (k + l) Bool S') (f : S \u2192 S') (htr : \u2200 q inp work, tm'.tr (f q) inp work = leftAction l f (tm.tr q inp (fun i => work (Fin.castAdd l i)))) (c : Cfg k Bool S x) (tapes : Fin l \u2192 \u2124 \u2192 Option Bool) (heads : Fin l \u2192 \u2124) (t : \u2115) : tm'.runFrom (leftCfg f c tapes heads) t = leftCfg f (tm.runFrom c t) tapes heads",
    "Turing.FinTM.leftCfg_step": "lemma leftCfg_step {k l : \u2115} {S S' : Type} {x : List Bool} (tm : MultiTapeTM k Bool S) (tm' : MultiTapeTM (k + l) Bool S') (f : S \u2192 S') (htr : \u2200 q inp work, tm'.tr (f q) inp work = leftAction l f (tm.tr q inp (fun i => work (Fin.castAdd l i)))) (c : Cfg k Bool S x) (tapes : Fin l \u2192 \u2124 \u2192 Option Bool) (heads : Fin l \u2192 \u2124) : tm'.step (leftCfg f c tapes heads) = leftCfg f (tm.step c) tapes heads",
    "Turing.FinTM.moveInputPos_neg_val": "lemma moveInputPos_neg_val {n : \u2115} (pos : Fin (n + 2)) : (moveInputPos pos .neg).val = pos.val - 1",
    "Turing.FinTM.rewind_from_any": "lemma rewind_from_any {k : \u2115} {S : Type} {x : List Bool} (tm : MultiTapeTM k Bool S) (start scan : S) (dest : Option S) (hstart : \u2200 inp work, tm.tr start inp work = controlAction .neg (some scan)) (hscan : \u2200 inp work, tm.tr scan inp work = match inp with | some _ => controlAction .neg (some scan) | none => controlAction .pos dest) (cfg : Cfg k Bool S x) (hs : cfg.state = some start) : \u2203 t, tm.runFrom cfg t = {cfg with state := dest, inputPos := 1}",
    "Turing.FinTM.rewind_heads": "theorem rewind_heads {k : \u2115} {S : Type} {x : List Bool} (tm : MultiTapeTM k Bool S) (start scan : S) (dest : Option S) (hstart : \u2200 inp work, tm.tr start inp work = controlAction .neg (some scan)) (hscan : \u2200 inp work, tm.tr scan inp work = match inp with | some _ => controlAction .neg (some scan) | none => controlAction .pos dest) (c : Cfg k Bool S x) (hs : c.state = some start) : \u2203 r \u2264 c.inputPos.val + 2, tm.runFrom c r = {c with state := dest, inputPos := 1} \u2227 \u2200 u \u2264 r, (tm.runFrom c u).workTapePos = c.workTapePos",
    "Turing.FinTM.rewind_scan": "lemma rewind_scan {k : \u2115} {S : Type} {x : List Bool} (tm : MultiTapeTM k Bool S) (scan : S) (dest : Option S) (htr : \u2200 inp work, tm.tr scan inp work = match inp with | some _ => controlAction .neg (some scan) | none => controlAction .pos dest) : \u2200 (cfg : Cfg k Bool S x), cfg.state = some scan \u2192 cfg.inputPos.val \u2264 x.length \u2192 tm.runFrom cfg (cfg.inputPos.val + 1) = {cfg with state := dest, inputPos := 1}",
    "Turing.FinTM.rewind_scan_heads": "theorem rewind_scan_heads {k : \u2115} {S : Type} {x : List Bool} (tm : MultiTapeTM k Bool S) (scan : S) (dest : Option S) (htr : \u2200 inp work, tm.tr scan inp work = match inp with | some _ => controlAction .neg (some scan) | none => controlAction .pos dest) : \u2200 (j : \u2115) (cfg : Cfg k Bool S x), cfg.state = some scan \u2192 cfg.inputPos.val = j \u2192 j \u2264 x.length \u2192 \u2200 u \u2264 j + 1, (tm.runFrom cfg u).workTapePos = cfg.workTapePos",
    "Turing.FinTM.rightAction": "def rightAction {l : \u2115} {S S' : Type} (k : \u2115) (f : S \u2192 S') (a : Action l Bool S) : Action (k + l) Bool S'",
    "Turing.FinTM.rightCfg": "def rightCfg {k l : \u2115} {S S' : Type} {x : List Bool} (f : S \u2192 S') (c : Cfg l Bool S x) (tapes : Fin k \u2192 \u2124 \u2192 Option Bool) (heads : Fin k \u2192 \u2124) : Cfg (k + l) Bool S' x",
    "Turing.FinTM.rightCfg_apply": "lemma rightCfg_apply {k l : \u2115} {S S' : Type} {x : List Bool} (f : S \u2192 S') (a : Action l Bool S) (c : Cfg l Bool S x) (tapes : Fin k \u2192 \u2124 \u2192 Option Bool) (heads : Fin k \u2192 \u2124) : (rightAction k f a).apply (rightCfg f c tapes heads) = rightCfg f (a.apply c) tapes heads",
    "Turing.FinTM.rightCfg_run": "lemma rightCfg_run {k l : \u2115} {S S' : Type} {x : List Bool} (tm : MultiTapeTM l Bool S) (tm' : MultiTapeTM (k + l) Bool S') (f : S \u2192 S') (htr : \u2200 q inp work, tm'.tr (f q) inp work = rightAction k f (tm.tr q inp (fun i => work (Fin.natAdd k i)))) (c : Cfg l Bool S x) (tapes : Fin k \u2192 \u2124 \u2192 Option Bool) (heads : Fin k \u2192 \u2124) (t : \u2115) : tm'.runFrom (rightCfg f c tapes heads) t = rightCfg f (tm.runFrom c t) tapes heads",

## ===== campaign/fills/mig1/inputs/search/INSPECTION.md =====

# Forwarding API candidate inspection

The fresh search enumerated **104 refs / 76 distinct TCSlib trees**, covering both open PRs,
prepared local/remote Lean heads and available delivery refs. Every ref/full commit/tree was
resolved and checked with Git. The three proposed full public names have **zero declaration
collisions** in those searched trees. This is candidate enumeration and inspection, not a
claim of semantic exhaustiveness.

The broad raw pattern deliberately overselects ordinary pairEncode uses, FP closure,
projections, padding and other unrelated formulas. All raw results are retained. Focused
formal-header candidates and the explicitly inspected existing time-only row are in
`formal-shape-candidates.json`.

| Actual reusable material | Disposition |
|---|---|
| Primitives' `computesFunInTime_pairMapSnd` | Existing existential time-only row; it supplies no named witness with the intrinsic space contract. The approved consolidation repoints this row. |
| Catalog's `computesFunInTime_pairMapSnd_spaceUsed` and private `a2_mapTM` | The canonical forwarding implementation and its time/space arguments; move these to the named witness's approved Primitives home, then make the existing row a corollary. No third implementation. |
| Catalog's strip-last candidates | Different function, with final-marker search and rejection; keep/use their existing named spec, not a second forwarding-map API. |
| Higher-level polynomial-time pairing/closure and ordinary pair-encoding applications | Consumers or different formulas; they are not another named forwarding machine or a proof of the two proposed same-witness specifications. No extra cleanup or new debt acknowledgment is inferred. |

The two open PRs add no forwarding API. NatBits overlaps Encoding and Catalog mechanically;
its diff does not implement the forwarding controller. SG-1 has no owned-file overlap. The
separate prepared Hierarchy consumer changes only Hierarchy's import/proof, with no forwarding
name or contract. The worker remains pinned; the maintainer handles later integration.

    (w₀.length + max u.length v.length + 3) * (n + 1)

Turing.copyTM_run_ofCfg.{u_1} {Symbol : Type u_1} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol} (src dst : Fin k) (hne : src ≠ dst)
  (w : List Symbol) (d : Cfg k Symbol SweepPhase x) (hstate : d.state = some SweepPhase.sweep)

  MultiTapeTM.runFrom d (2 * w.length + 2) =
      { state := some SweepPhase.done, inputPos := d.inputPos,
        workTapes := fun j q =>
          if j = dst ∧ d.workTapePos j ≤ q ∧ q < d.workTapePos j + ↑w.length then bufferTape w (q - d.workTapePos j)
          else d.workTapes j q,
        workTapePos := d.workTapePos, output := d.output } ∧
    (∀ t < 2 * w.length + 2, (MultiTapeTM.runFrom d t).state ≠ some SweepPhase.done) ∧
      ∀ (j : Fin k),
        ∀ t ≤ 2 * w.length + 2,
          if j = src ∨ j = dst then
            (MultiTapeTM.runFrom d t).workTapePos j ∈ Finset.Icc (d.workTapePos j - 1) (d.workTapePos j + ↑w.length)
          else (MultiTapeTM.runFrom d t).workTapePos j = d.workTapePos j

  (src dst : Fin k) (hdst : w dst = []) :
  (have __src := Cfg.ofWords q w;

        if j = dst ∧ (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j ≤ p ∧ p < (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j + ↑(w src).length then

      workTapes := fun j p =>
        if j = src ∧ (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j ≤ p ∧ p < (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j + ↑(w src).length then

  ((MultiTapeTM.runFrom (MultiTapeTM.initCfg x) t).state =
      match (MultiTapeTM.runFrom (MultiTapeTM.initCfg x) t).state with
      | some s => some (Sum.inl (s, (MultiTapeTM.runFrom (MultiTapeTM.initCfg x) t).output.getLast?))
      | none =>
        if (MultiTapeTM.runFrom (MultiTapeTM.initCfg x) t).output.getLast? = some haltOn then none
        else some (Sum.inr ())) ∧
    (MultiTapeTM.runFrom (MultiTapeTM.initCfg x) t).inputPos =
        (MultiTapeTM.runFrom (MultiTapeTM.initCfg x) t).inputPos ∧
      (MultiTapeTM.runFrom (MultiTapeTM.initCfg x) t).workTapes =
          (MultiTapeTM.runFrom (MultiTapeTM.initCfg x) t).workTapes ∧
        (MultiTapeTM.runFrom (MultiTapeTM.initCfg x) t).workTapePos =
            (MultiTapeTM.runFrom (MultiTapeTM.initCfg x) t).workTapePos ∧
          (MultiTapeTM.runFrom (MultiTapeTM.initCfg x) t).output = []

Turing.FinTM.timed_rewind {k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool} (tm : MultiTapeTM k Bool S) (start scan : S)
  (dest : Option S)
  (hstart :
    ∀ (inp : Option Bool) (work : Fin k → Option Bool), tm.tr start inp work = controlAction SignType.neg (some scan))
  (hscan :
    ∀ (inp : Option Bool) (work : Fin k → Option Bool),
      tm.tr scan inp work =
        match inp with
        | some val => controlAction SignType.neg (some scan)
        | none => controlAction SignType.pos dest)
  (c : Cfg k Bool S x) (hs : c.state = some start) :
  ∃ r ≤ ↑c.inputPos + 2,
    MultiTapeTM.runFrom c r =
      { state := dest, inputPos := 1, workTapes := c.workTapes, workTapePos := c.workTapePos, output := c.output }

  (dest : Option S)
  (hstart :
    ∀ (inp : Option Bool) (work : Fin k → Option Bool), tm.tr start inp work = controlAction SignType.neg (some scan))
  (hscan :
    ∀ (inp : Option Bool) (work : Fin k → Option Bool),
      tm.tr scan inp work =
        match inp with
        | some val => controlAction SignType.neg (some scan)
        | none => controlAction SignType.pos dest)
  (cfg : Cfg k Bool S x) (hs : cfg.state = some start) :
  ∃ t,
    MultiTapeTM.runFrom cfg t =
      { state := dest, inputPos := 1, workTapes := cfg.workTapes, workTapePos := cfg.workTapePos, output := cfg.output }

Turing.copyTM_run_ofCfg.{u_1} {Symbol : Type u_1} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol} (src dst : Fin k) (hne : src ≠ dst)
  (w : List Symbol) (d : Cfg k Symbol SweepPhase x) (hstate : d.state = some SweepPhase.sweep)
  (hw : ∀ (p : ℤ), -1 ≤ p → p ≤ ↑w.length → d.workTapes src (d.workTapePos src + p) = bufferTape w p) :
  MultiTapeTM.runFrom d (2 * w.length + 2) =
      { state := some SweepPhase.done, inputPos := d.inputPos,
        workTapes := fun j q =>
          if j = dst ∧ d.workTapePos j ≤ q ∧ q < d.workTapePos j + ↑w.length then bufferTape w (q - d.workTapePos j)
          else d.workTapes j q,
        workTapePos := d.workTapePos, output := d.output } ∧
    (∀ t < 2 * w.length + 2, (MultiTapeTM.runFrom d t).state ≠ some SweepPhase.done) ∧
      ∀ (j : Fin k),
        ∀ t ≤ 2 * w.length + 2,
          if j = src ∨ j = dst then
            (MultiTapeTM.runFrom d t).workTapePos j ∈ Finset.Icc (d.workTapePos j - 1) (d.workTapePos j + ↑w.length)
          else (MultiTapeTM.runFrom d t).workTapePos j = d.workTapePos j
Turing.transferTM_run_ofCfg.{u_1} {Symbol : Type u_1} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol} (src dst : Fin k) (hne : src ≠ dst)
  (w : List Symbol) (d : Cfg k Symbol SweepPhase x) (hstate : d.state = some SweepPhase.sweep)
  (hw : ∀ (p : ℤ), -1 ≤ p → p ≤ ↑w.length → d.workTapes src (d.workTapePos src + p) = bufferTape w p) :
  MultiTapeTM.runFrom d (2 * w.length + 2) =
      { state := some SweepPhase.done, inputPos := d.inputPos,
        workTapes := fun j q =>
          if j = src ∧ d.workTapePos j ≤ q ∧ q < d.workTapePos j + ↑w.length then none
          else
            if j = dst ∧ d.workTapePos j ≤ q ∧ q < d.workTapePos j + ↑w.length then bufferTape w (q - d.workTapePos j)
            else d.workTapes j q,
        workTapePos := d.workTapePos, output := d.output } ∧
    (∀ t < 2 * w.length + 2, (MultiTapeTM.runFrom d t).state ≠ some SweepPhase.done) ∧
      ∀ (j : Fin k),
        ∀ t ≤ 2 * w.length + 2,
          if j = src ∨ j = dst then
            (MultiTapeTM.runFrom d t).workTapePos j ∈ Finset.Icc (d.workTapePos j - 1) (d.workTapePos j + ↑w.length)
          else (MultiTapeTM.runFrom d t).workTapePos j = d.workTapePos j
Turing.Cfg.ofWords_copy_endpoint.{u_1} {k : ℕ} {S : Type u_1} {x : List Bool} (q q' : S) (w : Fin k → List Bool)
  (src dst : Fin k) (hdst : w dst = []) :
  (have __src := Cfg.ofWords q w;
    { state := some q', inputPos := __src.inputPos,
      workTapes := fun j p =>
        if j = dst ∧ (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j ≤ p ∧ p < (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j + ↑(w src).length then
          bufferTape (w src) (p - (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j)
        else (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapes j p,
      workTapePos := __src.workTapePos, output := __src.output }) =
    Cfg.ofWords q' (Function.update w dst (w src))
Turing.Cfg.ofWords_transfer_endpoint.{u_1} {k : ℕ} {S : Type u_1} {x : List Bool} (q q' : S) (w : Fin k → List Bool)
  (src dst : Fin k) (hne : src ≠ dst) (hdst : w dst = []) :
  (have __src := Cfg.ofWords q w;
    { state := some q', inputPos := __src.inputPos,
      workTapes := fun j p =>
        if j = src ∧ (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j ≤ p ∧ p < (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j + ↑(w src).length then
          none
        else
          if j = dst ∧ (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j ≤ p ∧ p < (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j + ↑(w src).length then
            bufferTape (w src) (p - (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j)
          else (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapes j p,
      workTapePos := __src.workTapePos, output := __src.output }) =
    Cfg.ofWords q' (Function.update (Function.update w src []) dst (w src))
Turing.FinTM.callTM_run (M : FinTM Bool) (emit : Bool) (x arg cap : List Bool) (T : ℕ)
  (hM : M.ComputesInTime arg cap T) :
  ∃ t ≤ (24 + 13 * M.k) * (T + arg.length + cap.length + 1),
    0 < t ∧
      (∀ j < t,
          (MultiTapeTM.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (M.callEntry emit) (stateWord (M.callTM emit).k arg)) j).state ≠
            some (M.callExit emit)) ∧
        MultiTapeTM.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (M.callEntry emit) (stateWord (M.callTM emit).k arg)) t =
          have __src := Cfg.ofWords (M.callExit emit) (stateWord (M.callTM emit).k (if emit = true then arg else cap));
          { state := __src.state, inputPos := __src.inputPos, workTapes := __src.workTapes,
            workTapePos := __src.workTapePos, output := if emit = true then cap else [] }

Turing.copyTM_run_ofCfg.{u_1} {Symbol : Type u_1} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol} (src dst : Fin k) (hne : src ≠ dst)
  (w : List Symbol) (d : Cfg k Symbol SweepPhase x) (hstate : d.state = some SweepPhase.sweep)
  (hw : ∀ (p : ℤ), -1 ≤ p → p ≤ ↑w.length → d.workTapes src (d.workTapePos src + p) = bufferTape w p) :
  MultiTapeTM.runFrom d (2 * w.length + 2) =
      { state := some SweepPhase.done, inputPos := d.inputPos,
        workTapes := fun j q =>
          if j = dst ∧ d.workTapePos j ≤ q ∧ q < d.workTapePos j + ↑w.length then bufferTape w (q - d.workTapePos j)
          else d.workTapes j q,
        workTapePos := d.workTapePos, output := d.output } ∧
    (∀ t < 2 * w.length + 2, (MultiTapeTM.runFrom d t).state ≠ some SweepPhase.done) ∧
      ∀ (j : Fin k),
        ∀ t ≤ 2 * w.length + 2,
          if j = src ∨ j = dst then
            (MultiTapeTM.runFrom d t).workTapePos j ∈ Finset.Icc (d.workTapePos j - 1) (d.workTapePos j + ↑w.length)
          else (MultiTapeTM.runFrom d t).workTapePos j = d.workTapePos j

  (w : List Symbol) (d : Cfg k Symbol SweepPhase x) (hstate : d.state = some SweepPhase.sweep)

          if j = src ∧ d.workTapePos j ≤ q ∧ q < d.workTapePos j + ↑w.length then none
          else

            else d.workTapes j q,
        workTapePos := d.workTapePos, output := d.output } ∧
    (∀ t < 2 * w.length + 2, (MultiTapeTM.runFrom d t).state ≠ some SweepPhase.done) ∧

        ∀ t ≤ 2 * w.length + 2,
          if j = src ∨ j = dst then
            (MultiTapeTM.runFrom d t).workTapePos j ∈ Finset.Icc (d.workTapePos j - 1) (d.workTapePos j + ↑w.length)
          else (MultiTapeTM.runFrom d t).workTapePos j = d.workTapePos j
Turing.Cfg.ofWords_copy_endpoint.{u_1} {k : ℕ} {S : Type u_1} {x : List Bool} (q q' : S) (w : Fin k → List Bool)
  (src dst : Fin k) (hdst : w dst = []) :
  (have __src := Cfg.ofWords q w;
    { state := some q', inputPos := __src.inputPos,
      workTapes := fun j p =>
        if j = dst ∧ (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j ≤ p ∧ p < (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j + ↑(w src).length then
          bufferTape (w src) (p - (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j)
        else (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapes j p,
      workTapePos := __src.workTapePos, output := __src.output }) =
    Cfg.ofWords q' (Function.update w dst (w src))
Turing.Cfg.ofWords_transfer_endpoint.{u_1} {k : ℕ} {S : Type u_1} {x : List Bool} (q q' : S) (w : Fin k → List Bool)
  (src dst : Fin k) (hne : src ≠ dst) (hdst : w dst = []) :

      workTapes := fun j p =>
        if j = src ∧ (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j ≤ p ∧ p < (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j + ↑(w src).length then
          none
        else
          if j = dst ∧ (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j ≤ p ∧ p < (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j + ↑(w src).length then
            bufferTape (w src) (p - (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos j)
          else (Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapes j p,

  MultiTapeTM.runFrom d (2 * w.length + 2) =
      { state := some SweepPhase.done, inputPos := d.inputPos,
        workTapes := fun j q =>
          if j = src ∧ d.workTapePos j ≤ q ∧ q < d.workTapePos j + ↑w.length then none
          else
            if j = dst ∧ d.workTapePos j ≤ q ∧ q < d.workTapePos j + ↑w.length then bufferTape w (q - d.workTapePos j)

          if j = src ∨ j = dst then
            (MultiTapeTM.runFrom d t).workTapePos j ∈ Finset.Icc (d.workTapePos j - 1) (d.workTapePos j + ↑w.length)

## ===== campaign/fills/mig1/prepare.py =====

```
"""Prepare the pinned MIG-1 overnight fill inputs; no Lean source mutation.

Run with python3 -I after sourcing the scratch environment. The only checked
programs loaded here are the maintainer's declaration parser and graph tools.
"""

from pathlib import Path
import contextlib
import hashlib
import io
import json
import os
import re
import runpy
import subprocess
import sys
import tarfile

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SCRATCH = Path(os.environ['TCSLIB_SCRATCH'])

def git(*args):
    return subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(ROOT), *args], text=True).strip()

def checked(ref):
    sha = git('rev-parse', ref)
    subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(ROOT), 'cat-file', '-e', sha+'^{commit}'], check=True)
    return sha

def statement(text):
    # A header delimiter is top-level. In particular `input := x` in a
    # parenthesized configuration type is not the theorem's body delimiter.
    out=[];i=0;comment=0;quoted=False;depth=0
    while i<len(text):
        if text.startswith('/-',i) and not quoted:
            comment+=1;i+=2;continue
        if text.startswith('-/',i) and comment:
            comment-=1;i+=2;continue
        if comment:i+=1;continue
        if text.startswith('--',i) and not quoted:
            j=text.find('\n',i);i=len(text) if j<0 else j;continue
        c=text[i]
        if c=='"':quoted=not quoted
        if quoted and c=='\\' and i+1<len(text):
            out.extend(text[i:i+2]);i+=2;continue
        if not quoted:
            if c in '([{⟨':depth+=1
            elif c in ')]}⟩':depth-=1
            if depth==0 and (text.startswith(':=',i) or
                re.match(r'where\b',text[i:]) or c=='|'):
                return ' '.join(''.join(out).split())
        out.append(c);i+=1
    return ' '.join(''.join(out).split())

def main():
    base = checked('83ac315e')
    export = SCRATCH / 'mig1-source' / base
    export.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    proc = subprocess.Popen(['git', '-C', str(ROOT), 'archive', base, 'TCSlib',
                             'TCSlib.lean', 'scripts', 'devtools', 'policy.md',
                             'workflow.md', 'lean-toolchain', 'lake-manifest.json',
                             'lakefile.lean'], stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
    with tarfile.open(fileobj=proc.stdout, mode='r|') as a:
        a.extractall(export, filter='data')
    assert proc.wait() == 0
    # The export is a fresh materialization of this Git tree, not a worktree.
    paths = [
        'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Composition.lean',
        'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Simulation.lean',
        'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Wrappers.lean',
        'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Encoding.lean',
        'TCSlib/Complexity/ClassP/TimeConstructible.lean',
        'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Loop.lean',
        'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Primitives.lean',
        'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Catalog.lean',
        'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/CertShell.lean',
        'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/CodeSimulator.lean',
        'TCSlib/Complexity/RAMSimulation/WordSize.lean',
    ]
    inp = HERE / 'inputs'
    inp.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    empty = inp / 'empty.lean.txt'
    empty.write_text('')
    sys.argv = [str(ROOT/'devtools/seyoon/declfreeze.py'), str(empty), str(empty)]
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
        parser = runpy.run_path(sys.argv[0])
    chunks, stmt = parser['chunks'], statement
    rows, admissions, public = [], [], {}
    for path in paths:
        data = (export/path).read_bytes()
        blob = git('rev-parse', base+':'+path)
        subprocess.run(['git','-C',str(ROOT),'cat-file','-e',blob],check=True)
        assert hashlib.sha1(b'blob '+str(len(data)).encode()+b'\0'+data).hexdigest() == blob
        decls = chunks(data.decode())
        pub = {n: stmt(t) for n, priv, t in decls if not priv}
        public[path] = pub
        rows.append({'path': path, 'git_blob': blob, 'sha256': hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),
                     'lines': len(data.splitlines()), 'public_source': len(pub),
                     'private_source': sum(priv for _,priv,_ in decls)})
        for n, priv, t in decls:
            # Strip comments with the same reviewed parser as the screen.
            no_comments = re.sub(r'/\-.*?\-/', '', t, flags=re.S)
            no_comments = '\n'.join(l.split('--')[0] for l in no_comments.splitlines())
            if re.search(r'\bsorry\b',no_comments):
                admissions.append({'path': path, 'name': n, 'private': priv, 'statement': stmt(t)})
    targets = [a for a in admissions if a['path'] != paths[-1]]
    assert len(targets) == 17, [(a['path'], a['name']) for a in targets]
    assert len(admissions) == 20
    assert not any(a['private'] for a in admissions)
    retired = ['Turing.transferTM_run','Turing.copyTM_run','Turing.clearTM_run',
               'Turing.compareTM_run','Turing.incrementTM_run_succ','Turing.incrementTM_run_overflow']
    assert all(n in public[paths[7]] for n in retired)
    (inp/'owned-files.txt').write_text('\n'.join(paths)+'\n')
    (inp/'source-census.json').write_text(json.dumps({'base':base,'files':rows},indent=2)+'\n')
    (inp/'public-freeze.json').write_text(json.dumps(public,indent=2,sort_keys=True)+'\n')
    (inp/'base-admissions.json').write_text(json.dumps(admissions,indent=2)+'\n')
    (inp/'target-admissions.json').write_text(json.dumps(targets,indent=2)+'\n')
    (inp/'retired-public-names.txt').write_text('\n'.join(retired)+'\n')
    # Full screen populations include every Lean file named in this brief/probe.
    extra = [
        'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Configuration.lean',
        'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Deterministic.lean',
        'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Finite.lean',
        'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Convention.lean',
        'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Embed.lean',
    ]
    pop = list(dict.fromkeys(paths+extra))
    assert all((export/p).exists() for p in pop)
    (inp/'screen-population.txt').write_text('\n'.join(pop)+'\n')
    mods = {str(p.relative_to(export))[:-5].replace('/', '.'): p
            for p in (export/'TCSlib').rglob('*.lean')}
    imports = {m: re.findall(r'^import\s+(TCSlib\.[\w.]+)', p.read_text(), re.M)
               for m,p in mods.items()}
    cat = 'TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Catalog'
    prim = 'TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Primitives'
    # Only the already-approved TCSlib import addition. Validate its direction.
    imports[cat] = list(dict.fromkeys(imports[cat]+[prim]))
    order, seen, active = [], set(), set()
    def visit(m):
        assert m in mods, m
        assert m not in active, ('cycle',m,active)
        if m in seen: return
        active.add(m)
        for dep in sorted(imports[m]): visit(dep)
        active.remove(m)
        seen.add(m)
        order.append(m)
    for p in pop: visit(p[:-5].replace('/','.'))
    (inp/'bootstrap-order.txt').write_text(''.join(m.replace('.','/')+'\n' for m in order))
    roots = set()
    for m in order:
        roots.update(re.findall(r'^import\s+(Mathlib\.[\w.]+)',mods[m].read_text(),re.M))
    roots.add('Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin')
    (inp/'mathlib-roots.txt').write_text('\n'.join(sorted(roots))+'\n')
    rev = {}
    for m,deps in imports.items():
        for d in deps: rev.setdefault(d,set()).add(m)
    down, todo = set(), [p[:-5].replace('/','.') for p in paths]
    while todo:
        m=todo.pop()
        if m in down:continue
        down.add(m);todo.extend(rev.get(m,()))
    down.discard('TCSlib')
    dorder=[];dseen=set()
    def dvisit(m):
        if m in dseen:return
        dseen.add(m)
        for dep in sorted(imports[m]):
            if dep in down:dvisit(dep)
        dorder.append(m)
    for m in sorted(down):dvisit(m)
    (inp/'downstream-order.txt').write_text(''.join(m.replace('.','/')+'\n' for m in dorder))
    # A fresh fill host also needs the unaffected imports of affected modules.
    # Keep the small 51-module proof-work bootstrap separate from that complete
    # final sweep, and fetch roots for both before the initial bootstrap.
    order=[];seen=set();active=set()
    for m in sorted(down):visit(m)
    final_order=order.copy()
    (inp/'final-order.txt').write_text(''.join(m.replace('.','/')+'\n' for m in final_order))
    roots=set()
    for m in final_order:
        roots.update(re.findall(r'^import\s+(Mathlib\.[\w.]+)',mods[m].read_text(),re.M))
    roots.add('Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin')
    (inp/'mathlib-roots.txt').write_text('\n'.join(sorted(roots))+'\n')
    # Static admission census for the bootstrap and downstream, without claiming
    # any new elaboration. Both lists are regenerated on the delivery by worker.
    base_sorries={}
    for m in final_order:
        names=[]
        for n,_,t in chunks(mods[m].read_text()):
            t=re.sub(r'/\-.*?\-/','',t,flags=re.S)
            t='\n'.join(l.split('--')[0] for l in t.splitlines())
            if re.search(r'\bsorry\b',t):names.append(n)
        if names:base_sorries[m]=names
    (inp/'closure-base-admissions.json').write_text(json.dumps(base_sorries,indent=2)+'\n')
    # Source-side candidate list for all six approved retirements, including docs.
    hits=[]
    pattern=re.compile(r'\b(?:'+ '|'.join(re.escape(n.split('.')[-1]) for n in retired)+r')\b')
    for m,p in sorted(mods.items()):
        for i,line in enumerate(p.read_text().splitlines(),1):
            if pattern.search(line):hits.append(f'{p.relative_to(export)}:{i}: {line}')
    (inp/'retirement-consumers.txt').write_text('\n'.join(hits)+'\n')
    refs=[]
    for ref in ['origin/complexity/arora-barak-ch3-4','origin/lean/dedup-sg1',
                'origin/lean/dedup-natbits','origin/lean/epad-padding-fill']:
        sha=checked(ref)
        changed=git('diff','--name-only',base+'...'+sha,'--','*.lean').splitlines()
        refs.append({'ref':ref,'commit':sha,'owned_overlap':sorted(set(paths)&set(changed))})
    (inp/'open-pr-overlap.json').write_text(json.dumps(refs,indent=2)+'\n')
    meta={'base':base,'export':str(export),'owned_files':len(paths),'target_admissions':len(targets),
          'screen_files':len(pop),'bootstrap_modules':len((inp/'bootstrap-order.txt').read_text().splitlines()),
          'downstream_modules':len(dorder),'final_modules':len(final_order),
          'mathlib_roots':len(roots),'catalog_primitives_edge_acyclic':True}
    (inp/'pins.json').write_text(json.dumps(meta,indent=2)+'\n')
    print(json.dumps(meta,indent=2))

if __name__=='__main__':main()
```

## ===== campaign/fills/mig1/review/brief-review.md =====

# MIG-1 megafill brief review

Independent internal source/brief review by Codex; no Lean, cache, build, screen, Git mutation,
commit or push was run by this reviewer. Only this review file was written. This is not the
external fill gate and does not certify the future delivery.

Reviewed brief: `campaign/fills/mig1/briefs/megafill-mig1.md`, SHA-256
`af596548bd09c26c0b0379362cbf8da0b86b34fdd0fbc999729efff66ff1a1ea`. Pinned proof base: `83ac315ed9e7089466bd16a32f3b71fbadc556d2`.
The author incorporated the two editorial findings below during this review; both corrections
were reread in the reviewed version.

**Verdict: 0 blockers, 0 majors, 0 open minors; 2 resolved minors, 4 notes.** The scope and
contracts support the proposed integrated overnight job. Finish the pending issue receipts
before describing the packet as ready to dispatch.

## Findings and dispositions

| ID | Severity | Location | Finding and evidence | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | minor, resolved | Delivery, checkpoint archive contents | The initial wording required both complete screens in every checkpoint, potentially delaying publication of early checked source until an expensive final screen/sweep. That weakened the recovery purpose of the checkpoints. | Fixed in the reviewed brief: early archives contain completed checks and explicit NOT RUN entries; the final complete delivery requires fresh complete screens and the full sweep. Validation-incomplete work remains a partial. |
| M2 | minor, resolved | F-B work package | The initial phrase “already proved” for existing strip/split/composite specs blurred supplied proof bodies with admission-free theorems. Gate 16 round 2 decision 2 explicitly makes strip depend on F-A and the split proofs depend on F-C plus the length counter. | Fixed: existing proof bodies are admission-free only after those dependencies are filled, with actual axiom verification required before claiming completion. |
| N1 | note, issue receipt | New forwarding exports and dispatch metadata | WORKFLOW §3 requires a fresh name/statement-shape search on open PRs, prepared landings and delivery refs before a new API pack. `open-pr-overlap.json` proves only file overlaps. The author confirmed that the separate candidate search/inspection receipt is being added. Final bundle/source/records pins and published-blob verification must likewise be recorded at issue. | Complete those evidence receipts before issue; no new design approval is needed for the three already-gated exports. |
| N2 | note, issue receipt | Pre-ship / baseline screen | The brief correctly distinguishes conditional route checks from proofs of the 17 existing targets and two future map theorems. During review the author was correcting a harmless unused-tactic warning and completing the 16-file baseline screen. `preship.json` must point to the final successful source/run hashes and the completed screen receipt. | Reconcile final hashes/exit counts and bundle all named inputs. Historical failed probes remain clearly labeled. No unrun seal, replay or source proof is certified by this review. |
| N3 | note, accepted | Ownership, public surface and temporary moves | The 11-file ownership is disjoint from the paused record-table rows, F6 and Ladner; WordSize is documentation-only. Exactly 17 existing specification admissions and exactly three future forwarding exports are identified. The six canonical public removals and their consumers match the final statement-gate plan. Temporary duplication of moved arguments until F-D is the already acknowledged scheduled migration in gate 16 note N8, with disclosure and one final home required. | Accepted. No additional interface/import/debt ruling is inferred. A missing cross-file API correctly yields an explicit gap/partial instead of a new private host. |
| N4 | note, accepted | Work order, helpers and current names | The F-A → F-C → F-B → F-D order matches design §9's allowed integrated execution. This is one fill with four packages, so the single cumulative branch is coherent with the explicit cover clarification. The approved Simulation BigOperators import and Catalog→Primitives edge are correctly limited. `callTM_run` supersedes the draft install/emit names; the primitive interval theorem and Simulation's existing space-from-time lemma are reused. | Accepted. Preserve the final coefficients and machine bodies; the contract file is historical statement data, so its old landing/provenance labels must not be copied into public Lean docstrings (the bundled policy already requires this). |

## Read-only cross-checks

- Read the maintainer entry/rules/current state, repository policy/workflow, environment addendum
  v2.6, MIG-1 design/inventory, final gate 16 pack/findings/resolutions, MIG-24 triage, the brief
  and current inputs/receipts. Historical measurements are treated as historical evidence.
- Compared all **11** owned-file input hashes and bytes with Git objects at the pinned base and
  the prepared source export; all match.
- Confirmed **17** target admission records, with the three unrelated RAM admissions excluded
  from that target set and frozen by the scope.
- Independently checked list cardinality, distinctness and dependency order for **51** bootstrap,
  **394** affected-downstream and **641** full-final modules, including the approved
  Catalog→Primitives import edge. The bootstrap and final lists contain their prerequisite
  TCSlib imports; the downstream list is correctly only the affected subset.
- Recomputed the exact union of direct Mathlib imports in the full final order plus the approved
  optional BigOperators import: **239 roots**, equal to the supplied root list.
- Checked the forwarding contract against the final gate's Primitives part: it contains exactly
  `Turing.FinTM.pairMapSndTM`, `_computes` and `_spaceUsed`, with forwarding mode true,
  coefficient 22, monotone time/space premises and coefficient one on the payload space. These
  are gated future additions, not exports claimed to exist in the proof base.

No source tactic correctness or future compilation claim is made. The eventual delivery still
needs the brief's complete freeze, source/compiled censuses, axiom walks, controls, screens and
current-campaign maintainer replay.

## ===== campaign/fills/mig1/review/resolutions.md =====

# Brief review dispositions

Original internal review retained verbatim, SHA-256 `2c49ce24578fac47a8455f737c172612b7a223faa88d452f9f7561d1e2e05344`.
The reviewed brief's SHA-256 `af596548bd09c26c0b0379362cbf8da0b86b34fdd0fbc999729efff66ff1a1ea` still matches the final brief.
No blocker, major or open minor remains.

- M1: fixed; early checkpoint archives carry completed checks plus explicit NOT RUN entries;
  both final screens and the full final sweep are required for a complete delivery.
- M2: fixed; existing proof bodies are called admission-free only after their dependencies close.
- N1: completed by the 104-ref/76-tree name/shape enumeration and candidate inspection. Exact
  publication/bundle pins follow in the dispatch receipt, after the package is actually pushed.
- N2: completed: final successful normal/sealed probe sources and run hashes reconcile, seven
  conditional axiom prints are standard; the two equation controls have exact expected exits.
  The completed full 16-file screen has 1,279 declarations / 1,589 pairs / 636,810 reproduced chars.
- N3/N4: accepted; no additional design/import/debt approval is inferred, and historical proposal
  names/provenance do not become public Lean prose.

This internal brief review is not the future delivery's external fill gate.

```
"""Run the reviewed conditional route and its one-definition seal/controls."""
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import time

h=Path(__file__).resolve().parent;r=h.parents[2];s=Path(os.environ['TCSLIB_SCRATCH'])
for name,expected,errors in [('RouteProbe',0,0),('RouteProbe-sealed',0,0),
                             ('ControlsUnsealed',0,0),('ControlsSealed',1,2)]:
    source=h/'inputs'/f'{name}.lean.txt'
    target=s/'mig1-probes'/f'{name}.lean'
    target.write_bytes(source.read_bytes())
    cmd=['bash',str(r/'devtools/seyoon/leanelab.sh'),str(s/'wt-camp'),
         str(s/'oleans-mac0'),str(target)]
    start=time.time()
    with (h/'logs'/f'{name}.out').open('w') as out:
        p=subprocess.run(cmd,stdout=out,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    output=(h/'logs'/f'{name}.out').read_text()
    diagnostic_errors=output.count('error:')+output.count('error(')
    receipt={'command':cmd,'exit':p.returncode,'expected_exit':expected,
             'errors':diagnostic_errors,'expected_errors':errors,'seconds':time.time()-start,
             'input_sha256':hashlib.sha256(source.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}
    (h/'logs'/f'{name}-run.json').write_text(json.dumps(receipt,indent=2)+'\n')
    assert p.returncode==expected and diagnostic_errors==errors,(name,output)
    if expected==0:assert 'sorryAx' not in output and 'warning:' not in output,(name,output)
    print(name,'passed expected result',flush=True)
```

## ===== campaign/fills/mig1/run-screen.py =====

```
"""One serialized base screen for the MIG-1 dispatch, with a source receipt."""
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import time

here=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
root=here.parents[2]
scratch=Path(os.environ['TCSLIB_SCRATCH'])
pins=json.loads((here/'inputs/pins.json').read_text())
pop=(here/'inputs/screen-population.txt').read_text().splitlines()
lock=scratch/'locks/screen'
while True:
    try:
        lock.mkdir()
        break
    except FileExistsError:
        time.sleep(5)
(lock/'pid').write_text(str(os.getpid())+'\n')
logs=here/'logs'
logs.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
cmd=['nice','-n','10','python3','-I',str(root/'scripts/copy-text-screen-v3.py'),pins['export'],*pop]
t=time.time()
try:
    with (logs/'screen-base.txt').open('w') as out:
        result=subprocess.run(cmd,stdout=out,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    receipt={'command':cmd,'base':pins['base'],'files':pop,'exit':result.returncode,
             'seconds':time.time()-t,
             'output_sha256':hashlib.sha256((logs/'screen-base.txt').read_bytes()).hexdigest()}
    (logs/'screen-base-run.json').write_text(json.dumps(receipt,indent=2)+'\n')
    assert result.returncode==0
    print((logs/'screen-base.txt').read_text().splitlines()[0],flush=True)
finally:
    assert (lock/'pid').read_text().strip()==str(os.getpid())
    (lock/'pid').unlink()
    lock.rmdir()
```

## ===== campaign/fills/mig1/search-api.py =====

```
"""Enumerate current forwarding-map API names/shapes across available refs.

This is candidate enumeration plus source inspection, never an exhaustiveness
proof. No checkout, fetch, source edit or Lean execution is performed.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import contextlib
import io
import json
import re
import runpy
import subprocess
import sys

h=Path(__file__).resolve().parent;r=h.parents[2];out=h/'inputs/search';out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
def git(*args):return subprocess.check_output(['git','-C',str(r),*args],text=True).strip()
prefixes=('refs/heads/lean/','refs/remotes/origin/lean/','refs/deliver/',
          'refs/heads/deliver/','refs/remotes/origin/deliver/',
          'refs/heads/archive/mac/','refs/remotes/origin/archive/mac/')
refs=[x for x in git('for-each-ref','--format=%(refname)').splitlines() if x.startswith(prefixes)]
refs+=['origin/complexity/arora-barak-ch3-4','83ac315e']
for p in json.loads((h/'inputs/open-prs.json').read_text()):
    refs+=['origin/'+p['headRefName']]
by_tree={};receipt=[]
for ref in sorted(set(refs)):
    sha=git('rev-parse',ref)
    subprocess.run(['git','-C',str(r),'cat-file','-e',sha+'^{commit}'],check=True)
    tree=git('rev-parse',sha+':TCSlib')
    subprocess.run(['git','-C',str(r),'cat-file','-e',tree+'^{tree}'],check=True)
    receipt.append({'ref':ref,'commit':sha,'tcslib_tree':tree})
    by_tree.setdefault(tree,sha)
pattern=r'pairMapSndTM|fwdMapTM|a2_mapTM|pairMapSnd_spaceUsed|pairEncode.*\([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z_0-9]* [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z_0-9]*\)'
sys.argv=[str(r/'devtools/seyoon/declfreeze.py'),str(h/'inputs/empty.lean.txt'),str(h/'inputs/empty.lean.txt')]
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):parser=runpy.run_path(sys.argv[0])
names={'Turing.FinTM.pairMapSndTM','Turing.FinTM.pairMapSndTM_computes','Turing.FinTM.pairMapSndTM_spaceUsed'}
hits={};collisions=[]
for tree,sha in by_tree.items():
    p=subprocess.run(['git','-C',str(r),'grep','-n','-E',pattern,sha,'--','TCSlib'],text=True,capture_output=True)
    assert p.returncode in (0,1),p.stderr
    (out/(sha+'.txt')).write_text(p.stdout)
    rows=p.stdout.splitlines();hits[sha]={'tree':tree,'candidate_lines':len(rows)}
    files={line.split(':',2)[1] for line in rows}
    for path in sorted(files):
        text=git('show',sha+':'+path)
        for n,private,body in parser['chunks'](text):
            if n in names and not private:
                collisions.append({'commit':sha,'path':path,'name':n})
(out/'refs.json').write_text(json.dumps(receipt,indent=2)+'\n')
(out/'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps({'ref_count':len(receipt),'unique_tcslib_trees':len(by_tree),
    'pattern':pattern,'trees':hits,'public_name_candidates':collisions,
    'method':'Candidate enumeration, followed by declaration-kind/name inspection; not an exhaustive semantic duplication proof.'},indent=2)+'\n')
print('Searched',len(receipt),'refs /',len(by_tree),'distinct TCSlib trees; public-name candidates:',len(collisions))
for c in collisions:print(c)
```

## ===== campaign/items/mig1/MIG1-design.md =====

# MIG-1 design: named witnesses, the `f2_` deletion, the R3 canonical retirement

> **Maintainer note (2026-10-13).** A maintainer sub-agent wrote this file against the read-only
> checkout `wt-mig1` of campaign commit `6aa9f67bc0b3181672d50eacb9d172e468070df3`. In the
> repository, `MIG1Draft.lean` is `audits/evidence/mig1/MIG1Draft.lean.txt`, `elaboration.log` is
> `audits/logs/mig1-draft-elaboration.log`, and the measurement scripts `work/*.py` are
> `audits/evidence/mig1/scripts/`; their data files are not kept. MIG-0a has since landed
> (PR #83) with the imports cited here, and MIG-0b's gate is issued (`audits/mig0b-pack.md`).

Statement-phase design for backlog row MIG-1 (`machine-library-design.md` §16, order of work
step 2), drafted 2026-10-13 against the campaign tip in `wt-mig1`. Measurements are in
`MIG1-inventory.md` (cited as *Inv.* §n); the representative statement draft is
`MIG1Draft.lean`, which elaborates with 0 errors and 26 `sorry` warnings (`elaboration.log`).
Figures marked ESTIMATE are estimates; all others are measured.

## 0. Summary

* **What MIG-1 does.** Every existential machine row of the eight named files (53 rows, plus
  `Complexity.timeConstructible_id`, whose definition hides the same existential; *Inv.* §1)
  gets a named public witness with spec theorems, and becomes a one-line corollary with its
  statement unchanged. The 304 `f2_` copies, the 45 `a2_` and the 7 `catalog_redirect*`
  declarations leave `Build/Catalog.lean`: the copies are deleted, and the new space proofs among
  them move next to their witnesses. The 20 Catalog space rows become short corollaries in place.
  The six R3 canonical `_run` rows retire, with their five consumer citations edited.
* **Witnesses:** 26 new public definitions (24 machines and the call's two anchor states), plus
  spec theorems for 2 existing public machines (`bufferedCompTM`, `redirectTM`): 28 in all
  (§3). 51 spec theorems and 4 supporting lemmas (ESTIMATE until stage S fixes the list; §3).
* **Style decision:** spec theorems in the library's existing style, not as MIG-0a `Contract`
  instances (§2).
* **Size:** net about −7.4k lines (ESTIMATE, range −6.9k to −7.8k; §12), against the backlog's
  −7.6k to −8.3k plus 0.4k: about 2.4k of the region's lines are new proofs that move rather than
  go. Catalog shrinks from 12,752 to about 3.3k lines (ESTIMATE).
* **Measured figures** against the backlog: 304 copies and 22 region publics reproduce; 66 rows,
  6,255 verbatim lines and "0 external consumers" of the R3 rows do not (*Inv.* §0).

## 1. Scope and invariants

**Rule.** Design §2: constructive layers export named machines with spec theorems; existential
packaging appears only at the consumer layer. §16 decision 1 lifts §8's byte-identity and
decision 12.2's byte-identical `Primitives`; decision 2 (scenario B) retires the R3 canonical
`_run` rows with their consumers edited.

**Invariants.**
1. Every one of the 53 rows and `timeConstructible_id` keeps its statement byte for byte, its
   name and its home module. Their 221 external citations in 35 files (*Inv.* §1) are untouched.
2. Witness bodies are moved or renamed, never changed (code identity modulo the rename map).
3. No row is ever proved through a `sorry`: a row's proof is swapped onto its witness only once
   the witness's spec theorems are proved (§8).
4. The only retired public statements are the six R3 canonical `_run` rows.
5. Two public head lemmas, `rewind_scan_heads` and `rewind_heads`, move from Catalog to
   `TuringMachine/Simulation.lean` (next to `timed_rewind`, which they refine) with their full
   names unchanged, so their three consumers (*Inv.* §2.2) are untouched.

**Out of scope.** The framed R3 rows and `_spaceUsedByTape` rows (MIG-11 makes them Contract
instances); the other Build files' existential rows (CfgRecord 3, RecordTable 6, OracleSim 4,
InputCall 2, Zone 2, CertShell 1, EmitIterBody 1, InputLength 1, and in the core CodeSimulator 2,
MathlibBridge 2, Universal 4; *Inv.* §0 note a); MIG-9's
counter unification; TMSAT's private polynomial machine (*Inv.* §4).

## 2. Contract instances or the existing style: existing style

**Decision.** The spec theorems are stated in the existing style: `ComputesInTime` /
`ComputesFunInTime` with explicit constants, `spaceUsed` bounds from `initCfg`, and, for the
loop and the call, the existing `Cfg.ofWords` seam statements with their witnesses named. The
draft carries no copy of the MIG-0a contract file.

**Reasons.**
1. **Layering forbids it.** The MIG-0a file imports `Build/Catalog` and `Build/Seam`
   (`audits/evidence/mig0/Contract-proposed-r2.lean.txt`, lines 6–8). Catalog itself and five
   home files (Composition, Simulation, Wrappers, Encoding, Loop) are in Catalog's import
   closure, so they cannot import it. Primitives and TimeConstructible could today, but not once
   MIG-1's corollaries make Catalog import Primitives, and through it TimeConstructible
   (*Inv.* §4). The core contract module that `Loop` could import is MIG-0b item 4, still being
   drafted. Contract-shaped specs would make MIG-1 wait on MIG-0b and its gate, against §16's
   order of work (MIG-1 is step 2, "no new infrastructure"; Contract instances are step 3).
2. **The shapes do not fit.** 28 of the 34 home rows are whole-machine function computations
   from `initCfg` to a halt, judged by the output (*Inv.* §1). A `Contract` is a first-exit
   contract with a full endpoint configuration, an exact time and per-tape intervals through the
   endpoint. Today's proofs determine neither the endpoint's work tapes nor an exact halting time
   for most witnesses; a Contract instance would have to take `post := M.runFrom d time` and
   `time := Nat.find …`, which adds no content. The space rows bound `spaceUsed` at every time
   from `initCfg`, not inside an interval envelope.
3. **Named witnesses come first anyway.** A `Contract M …` needs a named `M`; an existential row
   cannot be one. MIG-1 is therefore a prerequisite of MIG-11 and MIG-17, not a competitor.
4. **The Contract-shaped rows are kept ready.** Only the call rows (seam to seam, first positive
   exit) and the loop's configuration family (a round structure, MIG-0b's round layer) have
   contract shape. `callTM_install` and `callTM_emit` keep today's positive-only cut; since the
   landed `callEntry` and `callExit` are distinct (different summands of the state type), the
   full cut follows, which is exactly MIG-0a's entry/exit case split (design §16a, round-1
   minor 5). MIG-17 then packages them without restating.

## 3. The named witnesses

Names are public, in `Turing.FinTM` unless stated; "today" is the private name the body comes
from (*Inv.* §1). Constants are today's, made explicit. `k` lemmas (`W.k = n`, `rfl`) accompany
every witness whose space corollary needs its tape count.

Two more public lemmas: `Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.spaceUsed_le` (Catalog, today's private
`f2_space_of_time`; proved in the draft) and a run form of `workTapePos_step_le`
(`MultiTapeTM.workTapePos_runFrom_le`, Simulation; today's private `f2_head_steps`, which
backlog F6-1(g) retires with MIG-1, and the form `h1Run_headBound` of F7-1(a)).

**Naming decisions.** Private names are kept where they read well and renamed where they carry
an origin tag: `catalogPrefixTM → prependTM`, `emitterTokenTM → unaryTokenTM`,
`emitterAppendTM → appendBitTM`, `emCallTM → callTM`, `loopHostM → loopHostTM` (the `forward`
flag stays inside: `emitLoopTM` is the forwarding instance), `Complexity.counterTM →
Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM`. The last is declared in `ClassP/TimeConstructible.lean` under its
`Turing.FinTM` name, outside the file's `Complexity` namespace, so that MIG-9 can move it into
`Build/` without renaming; it stays in TimeConstructible now because `timeConstructible_id` needs
it and Primitives imports TimeConstructible.

**Two consolidations** (statement-preserving, open question 2): `computesFunInTime_pairDup`
moves onto Encoding's `pairDiagTM`, which computes the same function with no work tapes, and
`pairDupTM` with its four private lemmas retires (138 lines); `computesFunInTime_pairMapSnd`
moves onto the forwarding controller that its own space row already uses, and the
captured-payload `pairMapTM` with its 15 private lemmas retires (447 lines; *Inv.* §4). The
second also removes a witness that the F2 gate showed cannot carry the space claim.

## 4. Each row as a corollary

Five patterns, all exercised in `MIG1Draft.lean`, whose `row_*` theorems prove `type_of% @row`
(the landed row's own type) from the specs:

* **A, one line:** `⟨W, c, W_computes⟩` (with `.mono` when the spec is stated per input).
* **B, space with no work tapes:** A plus `spaceUsed_zero_tapes_eq_zero _ _ W_k`.
* **C, space from time:** A plus `ComputesInTime.spaceUsed_le` and the tape count (pairFst,
  pairSnd, pairConcat, polyBits, pairLenCheck, stripLast: today's proofs already argue this way).
* **D, space from the witness's own spec:** `⟨W, c, W_computes, W_spaceUsed⟩`, with one
  constant for both clauses (lengthBits, polyUnary, pairMapSnd, cond, loop, splitSolve).
* **E, configuration level:** the loop and call rows instantiate `loopHostTM_contracts`,
  `callTM_install`, `callTM_emit`.

| Row | Pattern | In the draft |
|---|---|---|
| `computesFunInTime_id`, `_const`, `_ifEq`, `_prepend`, `_pairEncodeFixed`, `_pairValid`, `_incFixed`, `_pairDup`, `_unaryToken`, `_appendBit`, `Turing.computesFunInTime_pairEncode_diag` | A | id, const, pairDup, pairEncode_diag |
| `computesFunInTime_lengthBits`, `Complexity.timeConstructible_id` | A | both |
| `computesFunInTime_pairFst`, `_pairSnd`, `_pairConcat` | A over `_fst`/`_snd`/`_concat` | fst, snd |
| `computesFunInTime_polyUnary`, `_polyBits`, `_pairLenCheck`, `_stripLast`, `_splitSolve`, `_splitSolveWith`, `_pairMapSnd`, `_cond` | A, with an arithmetic `mono` where the row's bound is coarser | polyUnary, pairMapSnd, cond |
| `computesFunInTime_comp`, `exists_comp_on_image`, `exists_comp_partial`, `exists_cond`, `Turing.exists_codeTM` | A over the iff or composition spec | — |
| `exists_loopCfgTM`, `exists_loopTM`, `exists_loopFindTM`, `exists_emitLoopTM` | E / A | all but emitLoop |
| `exists_installCallTM`, `exists_emitCallTM` | E | both |

## 6. The space rows as corollaries

Of the region's 22 public declarations (*Inv.* §2.2), 20 are space rows and stay in Catalog,
each a corollary by pattern B, C or D (or the redirect form); their statements and names are
unchanged, and the four with external consumers (id, prepend, lengthBits, polyUnary: 5
citations in `Inclusions` and `Constructible`) are untouched. The two head lemmas move to
Simulation (§1, invariant 5). Seven witnesses carry their own space theorem, because their
space argument depends on their run structure: `lengthBitsTM`, `polyUnaryTM`, `pairMapSndTM`,
`timedCondTM` (with `branchTM_spaceUsed`), `splitSolveTM`, `loopHostTM` (two), and
`redirectTM` (through `redirectTM_runFrom`). The other 13 space rows need only time specs, the
tape count and `ComputesInTime.spaceUsed_le`. The scope note of `exists_loopTM_spaceUsed`
(round-1 note R10: no space clause for the configuration and find forms) is unchanged; the
find-mode budget theorem is public now because `splitSolveTM_spaceUsed` needs it, and is the
space clause R10 said would be commissioned by a consumer.

The six rows (237 lines) specialize the framed `_run_ofCfg` rows to `Cfg.ofWords` starts by a
`Cfg.ext` computation of about 20 lines each (*Inv.* §3). The backlog's "0 external consumers"

`transferTM_run` at `CertShell:585, 589, 602`. Plan:
1. Add two canonical-word lemmas to Catalog's Part 1, stated once instead of per routine: the

2. Each consumer site calls `copyTM_run_ofCfg`/`transferTM_run_ofCfg` and rewrites with the

3. Delete the six rows and their two docstring mentions in CertShell.

`CertShell` is closed (wave-1 gate); `CodeSimulator` belongs to the B5a continuations in flight,
so the site at `:1291` is edited only after B5a's continuation integrates (open question 1).

## 8. Order of work

1. **Stage S, statements (maintainer, one PR, statement gate).** The 26 definitions are made
   public under their final names by an asserted scripted rename in each home file (bodies
   unchanged); the spec theorems and the supporting lemmas are added; the two head lemmas move to
   Simulation. A spec whose proof is a citation of an existing private lemma is proved at once
   (for example `pairExtractTM_computes`, `pairValidTM_computes`, `incFixedTM_computes`,
   `prependTM_computes`); every other spec lands `sorry`. **No row's proof changes in stage S**,
   so no proved row comes to depend on a `sorry`. Gate evidence: the extension of
   `MIG1Draft.lean` to all 54 rows (every row a `type_of%` corollary of the gated specs), the code
   identity of each renamed body, the name screen re-run on the final list, and the acyclicity
   of the new import.
2. **Stage F, fills (four parallel batches, §9).** Each batch proves the sorried specs of its
   files, by moving a row's body into its spec (28 of the 34 home rows: all of Composition,
   Wrappers, Encoding and Loop, and 12 of Primitives, with `timeConstructible_id`) or by moving
   Catalog's proofs (the seven space specs, `branchTM_spaceUsed`, the six composite rows), then
   swaps each row onto its witness. The Catalog batch deletes the region and retires the R3 rows.
3. **Stage G, full gate.** Retired statements (the six R3 rows) and consumer edits; freeze,
   replay, axioms, duplication.

**Which witnesses first.** First the 16 whose specs are today's in-file proofs (witnesses 1–4,
6, 7, 9–12, 20, 21, 23–26), `bufferedCompTM`'s specs, and the time specs of 5, 8, 13 and 22:
relocations inside one file, which give named witnesses to 28 home rows and
`timeConstructible_id`. Next the lower-layer space specs
(`lengthBitsTM`, `timedCondTM`, `branchTM`, `redirectTM`), then `loopHostTM`'s space specs (the
risk concentration, §11 item 1), then the six composites (14–19), whose definitions use
witnesses 2, 5, 8, 9, 12, 13, 22 and 24 and whose split-search space needs the loop's budget
theorem. Catalog comes last, because every corollary there cites a home spec.

## 10. Gates and replay closure

* **Statement gate** (stage S). Population: the 26 definitions, 51 spec theorems
  (ESTIMATE), `ComputesInTime.spaceUsed_le`, the run-form head lemma, the two canonical-word
  lemmas, and the two moved head lemmas (statements unchanged). Checks: names and homes; each
  spec's fidelity to today's private proof; the `type_of%` corollary file over all 54 rows;
  witness code identity modulo the rename map; the name screen; the acyclic new import.
* **Full gate** (stage G). Freeze: every public statement of the ten edited files unchanged
  except the six retired rows and the gated additions. **Replay closure: the ten edited files
  and everything importing them, 205 of the 623 modules** (*Inv.* §4), including 61
  colleague-owned `CircuitComplexity` modules and `TimeHierarchy/Separation`, replayed but not
  edited. Axiom probe: the 54 rows, the 20 Catalog space rows and every new spec, the standard
  three only, no `sorryAx`. Duplication screen over the combined head: no moved declaration twice,
  no `f2_`/`a2_` name left.

## 11. Risks

1. **The loop family's re-targeting (highest).** The 21 modified loop copies come from an older
   `Loop` (before `loopHostM … forward findMode`); the moved space proofs (about 800 lines) cite
   them. Measured: after removing the prefix, the old and the current host definitions differ only
   in the signature (the `forward` flag) and the body-dispatch line, which today goes through
   `loopBodyDispatch` (Loop:552–563), a `bif forward then … else captureAction …` whose `false`
   branch is the old line. So `loopHostM body F anchor false findMode` is very likely
   definitionally the old host; at F-C's start a `rfl` bridge should be tried, keeping most moved
   proofs as they are. Otherwise the phase lemmas are re-targeted one by one.
2. **Axiom regression.** Swapping a row onto a sorried spec would put `sorryAx` under 216
   external citations. Avoided by invariant 3 and the stage order.
3. **Universes, `Type*` versus `Type`.** Every witness is a `FinTM Bool` (`FinTM : Type → Type 1`,
   states in `Type`); MIG-1 introduces no universe parameter and does not engage MIG-0a's `Type`
   decision or UNIV-1. The R3 framed rows are stated for `{Symbol : Type*}`; consumers moving from
   the `Bool` canonical rows instantiate `Symbol := Bool`.
4. **Name clashes.** Screened (*Inv.* §4): no proposed full name exists except as the witness
   being renamed in its own home; `Complexity.polyUnaryTM` (TMSAT, private) resolves first in its
   namespace. The screen is re-run at stage S on the gated names.
5. **The colleague files with `open Turing`.** `TimeHierarchy/Separation.lean` opens
   `Turing.FinTM`, so every new `Turing.FinTM` name becomes visible there unqualified;
   `CircuitComplexity/Advice.lean` has a `Turing.FinTM` section. None of them mentions any
   proposed short name, bare or `FinTM.`-qualified (*Inv.* §4); they are replayed, never edited.
   A name added at the gate must pass the same screen.
6. **The new import edge.** Eight Catalog importers newly see Primitives and TimeConstructible
   (20 public names); screened clean.
7. **Public definitions over private helpers.** `polyUnaryTM`, `polyBitsTM`, `pairLenCheckTM`,
   `stripLastTM`, `splitSolveTM`, `splitSolveWithTM` unfold to private machines
   (`catalogPolyUnaryTM`, `pairCountTM`, `rawStripTM`, `anyTrueTM`, `splitBodyTM`,
   `emitterP2BodyTM`). Lean accepts this outside the module system; consumers use the specs.
   Revisit if the `module` system is adopted.
8. **Explicit constants of the composites** (14–19) are computed at stage S from today's proofs;
   a wrong constant blocks a fill. Pre-ship check: elaborate each composite time spec's proof
   sketch, or prove it at stage S where it is glue over proved specs.
9. **`toCodeTM`'s tape-count argument.** Today's proof eliminates `hk : M.k = 1` by destructuring
   `M`; the definition must match `⟨_, Q, hQ, dQ, tm⟩, rfl`, and is noncomputable
   (`Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq`). Benefit: RD-3's open space clause of the coding step becomes a
   lemma about `toCodeTM`.
10. **In-flight work.** Only §7 touches an in-flight file (`CodeSimulator`); `RecordTable` and the
    B5a files are replayed, not edited.
11. **Policy.** The 26 new public definitions need docstrings opening with statement prose (most
    private witnesses already have one); the moved proofs carry their sketches.

Two of the rows today use witnesses that compute the same function as another row's witness:
`computesFunInTime_pairDup` (Primitives, `pairDupTM`, no work tapes) and
`Turing.computesFunInTime_pairEncode_diag` (Encoding, `pairDiagTM`, no work tapes) both compute
`x ↦ pairEncode x x` in linear time. And `computesFunInTime_pairMapSnd` uses the captured-payload
`pairMapTM`, while its Catalog space row uses a different machine, the forwarding controller
`a2_mapTM Mg true`, because the captured payload visits `|g b| + 1` capture cells (the F2 gate's
round-1 finding 4, quoted in the space row's docstring, Catalog:5885–5888).

## 2. The `f2_` region of `Build/Catalog.lean`

### 2.1 Layout

Catalog has 12,752 lines. Its three parts: Part 1 (lines 147–1777, namespace `Turing`: the R3
machines, the framed rows, the canonical rows); the region (1779–11361, namespace
`Turing.FinTM`); Part 3 (11371–12752, the §12.8 rows). The region, by category
(`decls.py`, `verbatim.py`; lines with docstrings):

| Category | Declarations | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| `f2_` copies with a same-named source in a home file | 257 | 5,606 |
| `f2_` declarations with no same-named source (new space proofs and glue) | 47 | 1,323 |
| `a2_` declarations (new: the forwarding map controller, 30; the loop head ledger, 15) | 45 | 1,196 |
| `catalog_redirect*` (copies of Wrappers' private `redirectState`/`Action`/`Cfg`/`_run` family) | 7 | 77 |
| Public declarations (§2.2) | 22 | 992 |
| Blank lines and section comments between declarations | — | 389 |
| **Region** | **378** | **9,583** |

Sources of the 257 named copies: Primitives 145, Loop 80, TimeConstructible 19, Wrappers 10,
Composition 3. The 25 that differ from their source are the loop-host family copied from an
older `Build/Loop.lean` (21: `f2_loopHost` and its phase lemmas; Loop has since generalized
`loopHost` to `loopHostM … forward findMode`, Loop:576–650) and four split-search lemmas
(`f2_splitBody_round`, `f2_splitSolve_of_body`, `_source`, `_closed`), changed to thread space.

No region declaration uses a public Catalog declaration from outside the region
(`deps.py`); inside it, the rows use `computesFunInTime_const_spaceUsed`,
`computesFunInTime_prepend_spaceUsed`, `computesFunInTime_pairSnd_spaceUsed`,
`computesFunInTime_lengthBits_spaceUsed`, `rewind_heads` and `rewind_scan_heads`.

## 4. Other measured facts the design relies on

* **Imports** (`imports.py`). Catalog imports `Build/Loop` and `TuringMachine/Encoding`, not
  `Build/Primitives`; its import closure contains `Simulation`, `Composition`, `Wrappers`,
  `Encoding` and `Loop`, but neither Primitives nor TimeConstructible. Primitives does not import
  Catalog, so the edge Catalog → Primitives is acyclic. Of Catalog's 28 importers, 8 do not yet
  import Primitives (`Constructible`,
  `RecordTable`, `CounterLoop`, `Scan`, `Zone`, `InputCall`, `CfgRecord`, `InputLength`); the
  20 public names of Primitives and TimeConstructible would become visible there, and none of
  the 8 declares or uses any of them.
* **Replay closure.** The ten files MIG-1 edits (`Simulation`, `Composition`, `Wrappers`,
  `Encoding`, `TimeConstructible`, `Loop`, `Primitives`, `Catalog`, `CertShell`,
  `CodeSimulator`) and everything importing them: **205 of 623 modules** (61 in
  `CircuitComplexity`, 45 in `SpaceComplexity`, 45 in `TuringMachine`, 19 in `ClassNP`). Without
  `Simulation`: 176; without `Simulation` and `Encoding`: 141.
* **Primitives' public surface** is exactly its 18 existential rows.
* **Witness retirement candidates** (`deps2.py`, privates reached only from one row):
  `computesFunInTime_pairMapSnd` reaches 16 such declarations (447 lines with docstrings:
  `pairMapTM`, `pairMap_computes`, `catalogPayload_computes`, `catalogPayload_length` and 12
  `map*` lemmas); `computesFunInTime_pairDup` reaches 5 (138 lines: `pairDupTM`,
  `pairDup_computes`, `pairDup_double`, `scanCopy_run`, `scanCopy_finish`).
* **Name screen** for the proposed public names (`fullnames.py`, `clash.py`; a namespace-aware
  index of 14,047 declarations of `TCSlib`). No proposed full name exists today except as the
  private witness being renamed or made public in its own home. One short name recurs:
  `Complexity.polyUnaryTM` (P, `ClassNP/TMSAT.lean:145`), in another namespace; TMSAT is in
  `namespace Complexity` with `open Turing` only, so its own private declaration keeps resolving
  first. `TimeHierarchy/Separation.lean` (`open Turing Turing.FinTM TimeHierarchy`) and the
  `CircuitComplexity` files (several `open Turing`; `Advice.lean` has a `namespace Turing.FinTM`
  section) contain no occurrence of any proposed short name, bare or `FinTM.`-qualified. None of
  the proposed short names occurs in the Mathlib sources of the checkout.
* **`TMSAT.lean:145`** declares its own private unary polynomial machine; whether it duplicates
  `catalogPolyUnaryTM` was not measured.
