Notation used in this report: `|x|` is list length; `n=|x|` where a length parameter is used; `k` is the relevant host's work-tape count; `T`, `R`, `C`, `e`, `TE`, `Tg`, and `Sg` retain their meanings in the audited statements (time bound, loop fuel, polynomial coefficient/degree, evaluator time, mapped-machine time and space); `u` is the fuel machine's first halting time in the preparation argument; `p(t)` denotes a work-head position in the interval-to-absolute-bound explanation. No other new mathematical notation is introduced.

+/-- Uniform seam positions and segment lengths confine the complete loop,
+including an accepting halt and all stationary later times. No round count
+occurs in the interval: every next segment restarts at a bounded seam.
+**Proof sketch.** Induction on the number of seams `N`. Within the first segment
+a head moves at most one cell per step from a seam of radius `H`, so it stays
+within `H + B`; an early halt is absorbing; otherwise continue from the next
+seam. With no seams left, the halted terminal is stationary. -/

+    (tm : MultiTapeTM k Bool S) (cfg : ℕ → Cfg k Bool S x) (N B H : ℕ)

+      (cfg j).workTapePos i ≤ H)

+    (hterminal : ∀ i, -((H + B : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ (cfg N).workTapePos i ∧
+      (cfg N).workTapePos i ≤ (H + B : ℕ))
+    (hsegment : ∀ j < N, ∃ u ≤ B,
+      (tm.runFrom (cfg j) u).state = none ∨ tm.runFrom (cfg j) u = cfg (j + 1)) :
+    ∀ t i, -((H + B : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ (tm.runFrom (cfg 0) t).workTapePos i ∧
+      (tm.runFrom (cfg 0) t).workTapePos i ≤ (H + B : ℕ) := by
+  induction N generalizing cfg with
+  | zero =>
+    intro t i
+    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt _ hend]
+    exact hterminal i
+  | succ N ih =>
+    intro t i
+    obtain ⟨u, hu, he⟩ := hsegment 0 (by omega)
+    have hs := hseam 0 (by omega) i
+    have hp (v : ℕ) (hv : v ≤ B) :
+        -((H + B : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ (tm.runFrom (cfg 0) v).workTapePos i ∧
+        (tm.runFrom (cfg 0) v).workTapePos i ≤ (H + B : ℕ) := by
+      have hh := Finset.mem_Icc.mp (mig0bStandIn_workTapePos_runFrom_mem_Icc tm (cfg 0) v i)
+      omega
+    by_cases ht : t ≤ u

+    · rw [show t = u + (t - u) by omega, MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add]
+      rcases he with he | he

+      (M.tm.runFrom (M.tm.initCfg x) t).workTapePos i ≤ B) (t : ℕ) :

## ===== campaign/gates/16-mig1-statements/pack-r2.md =====

# External audit pack — MIG-1, round 2: the statement gate's repairs and re-measurement

Round 2 of the MIG-1 statement gate. Round 1 (`audits/mig1-statements-findings.md`, attached
verbatim): **gate open, 0 blockers, 1 major, 3 minors**, no false public spec and no changed
machine transition. The round-1 pack and bundle are immutable and unchanged; this pack
supplements them. The gate closes on a round with **zero blockers and zero majors**. Record
findings in `audits/mig1-statements-r2-findings.md`.

**Campaign context.** The machine-library migration (`machine-library-design.md` §2, §16;
backlog MIG-1 with MIG-9, MIG-11, MIG-17, MIG-20), under the Arora-Barak chapters 3-4 plan.
MIG-1 gives every existential machine row of eight library files a named public witness with
spec theorems, makes each row a short corollary with its statement unchanged, deletes Catalog's
304 private `f2_` copies (with 45 `a2_` and 7 `catalog_redirect*` declarations), and retires the
six R3 canonical `_run` rows. Round 1's pack describes the unit, the probes and the plan; this
pack describes only what changed and what was re-measured.

**What did not change** (MEASURED). The unit `MIG1Statements.lean.txt` (2,950 lines), the
spec-probe tail, the bridge probe and the axiom-probe print list: the round-2 runner rebuilds
them from the round-1 templates at the tip and they are **byte-identical** to the round-1
artifacts. So are the 26 witnesses, the 45 statements, the 55 corollaries, the identity
manifest, the rename map and the moved-name map. None of the ten MIG-1 files changed since
round 1 (the same git blobs; provenance log).

**What changed underneath** (MEASURED, provenance log). The campaign moved from `1781a230`
(round 1) to the tip `99ad2f98` (`99ad2f9894121f45c79a27722d9466223be16473`):
- PRs #85 (RD-2, the formula kit) and #86 (stage 2, the RAM simulation) added 8 modules (632
  now); 6 of them import a MIG-1 file;
- the MIG-0b round-2 gate closed (`6b5345cb`; 0 blockers, 0 majors, 3 minors), so
  MIG-0b's landing set is final.

**Every round-2 check was run at `99ad2f98`**, read-only, against its olean snapshot `oleans-t1`,
Lean `v4.25.0`. In this pack `r2/` is `audits/evidence/mig1/gate/r2/`, and "the X log" is
`audits/logs/mig1-statements-r2-X.log`.

**Maintainer note (since the measurement; MEASURED at `dc891632`).** Two merges followed the
round-2 measurement:
- **H2-M** (PR #88) moved the step block out of `CodeSimulator.lean`, one of the ten MIG-1
  files. The R3 site `copyTM_run` (round 1: `:1295`) is now at `:1282`; CodeSimulator's staying
  declarations are freeze-checked unchanged, and nothing else measured here is in that file.
- **Hydroxyi's ARM merge** (`8c23f3bc`, pushed to the campaign branch) touches none of the ten
  files. It adds two code citations of `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_lengthBits`
  (`ClassPSPACE/TQBFHardVerifier.lean:247, 264`), whose statement MIG-1 keeps. The import
  graph grows to 706 modules, 282 of them in the ten files' downstream closure (with the ten).

MIG-1 S re-measures consumers, closures and line positions at its own landing base, as round 1
requires. MIG-0b's landing follows C1's (#87) and precedes MIG-1 S, so the head bound will be
MIG-0b's interval lemma in `Finite` (decision 3).

## Resolutions

1. **Finding 1 (major): the extended contract's preparation step was retargeted at a weaker
   lemma. Repaired** as the auditor preferred. Loop's private `loopHost_prepare` is
   strengthened in place, for both `forward` modes, with the fuel-head clause, and its two
   callers are adjusted. Catalog's extended contract replaces Loop's `loopHost_contracts` over
   surviving home lemmas only. **Demonstrated by elaboration** of
   `r2/overlay/LoopOverlay.lean.txt` (overlay log): exit 0, 0 errors, 0 sorries, every key
   declaration free of `sorryAx`. The fate is corrected.
2. **Finding 1, generalized.** The systematic retarget table `r2/data/retarget-table.tsv`
   covers 59 moving or absorbed declarations and their 215 region citations. It finds **no
   WEAKER or inaccessible case besides `loopHost_prepare`**. Lean checks (`r2/checks/`) restate
   every non-verbatim Loop-sourced copy and prove it from its retarget. Their negative control
   at the tip fails exactly at `loopHost_prepare` and at the contract replacement that round 1
   already planned (retarget log).
3. **Finding 2 (minor): the runner did not propagate failures; the builder accepted an empty
   template set. Repaired.** `r2/scripts/runall.sh` is rewritten: `set -euo pipefail`,
   statuses accumulated, every count compared with `expected-r2.json`, an exact identity
   control, an input precheck. `r2/scripts/build_unit.py` refuses bad template sets and writes
   atomically. Three negative controls (runner-negative-control log).
4. **Finding 3 (minor): the bundle lacked files its reproduction description names.
   Repaired.** `r2/BUNDLE-FILES.txt` lists the manifests, the templates,
   `campaign_style_lint.py`, `consumer-names.json`, the overlay, the checks and every log.
   `r2/EVIDENCE-MAP.tsv` maps each runner input to its repository file; the 36 round-1 inputs
   are checked byte for byte. The runner exits 2 before writing anything if an input is missing.
5. **Finding 4 (minor): three descriptions overstated their evidence.** The corrected
   sentences are below ("Corrected descriptions").

## Finding 1: the repair

**The strengthened lemma** (private, `Build/Loop.lean:1241`; overlay part 1). Its conclusion
gains one conjunct; the hypotheses and the `forward` parameter are unchanged:

```lean
    ∃ (c : Cfg F.k Bool F.State x) (t : ℕ),
      c.state = none ∧ c.output = Nat.bits (R x.length) ∧ t ≤ 5 * T x.length + 7 ∧
      (loopHostM body F anchor forward findMode).tm.runFrom
        ((loopHostM body F anchor forward findMode).tm.initCfg x) t = loopReady body F c ∧
      ∀ i, -(T x.length : ℤ) ≤ c.workTapePos i ∧ c.workTapePos i ≤ T x.length
```

The body is kept. The new branch is proved for the actual fuel endpoint
`c = F.tm.runFrom (F.tm.initCfg x) u`. Here `u ≤ T |x|` is the first halting time from
`loop_first_halt`. The interval lemma at the initial configuration, whose heads are at 0, gives
`-u ≤ c.workTapePos i ≤ u`. This is Catalog's own argument (`:7350–7354`), retargeted:

```lean
  · intro i
    have h := Finset.mem_Icc.mp
      (mig0bStandIn_workTapePos_runFrom_mem_Icc F.tm (F.tm.initCfg x) u i)
    have hh : -(u : ℤ) ≤ c.workTapePos i ∧ c.workTapePos i ≤ u := by
      simpa [c, MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init, Cfg.ofWords] using h
    omega
```

**The callers.** `Loop.lean:2116` lies inside the replaced contract, whose moved text
destructures the clause as `hfuel` (Catalog's own line). `Loop.lean:4805`, in
`exists_emitLoopTM`, discards it with one token: `⟨…, hprepare, -⟩`.

**The overlay** (`r2/overlay/LoopOverlay.lean.txt`, 5,743 lines). `r2/scripts/build_overlay.py`
builds it from the tip's files by asserted replacements only.
- **Part 1** (5,180 lines) is the tip's `Build/Loop.lean` verbatim with:
  - (a) the strengthened `loopHost_prepare` and the caller edits;
  - (b) a labelled stand-in, `private mig0bStandIn_workTapePos_runFrom_mem_Icc`. It is
    MIG-0b's `Turing.MultiTapeTM.workTapePos_runFrom_mem_Icc` (landing `Finite.lean:386–408`);
    only the name, the visibility, the namespace and the docstring differ
    (`standin-vs-mig0b.diff`). At landing it is dropped and each citation names the MIG-0b
    lemma. `workTapePos_step_le` and `runFrom_succ_eq_step'` are at the tip, so no further
    stand-in is needed;
  - (c) the moved loop-budget family `loopCall_heads`, `segment_heads`, `space_radius` and
    `seamed_space`: Catalog's text with `f2_` dropped, the head bound read through
    `Finset.mem_Icc.mp`, and a proof sketch added to each docstring;
  - (d) Catalog's extended `f2_loopHost_contracts`, moved over Loop's `loopHost_contracts`.
    Loop's docstring is kept and gains a paragraph on the extension. The statement and proof
    are Catalog's under these retargets:
    - `f2_loopHost body F anchor findMode ↦ loopHost body F anchor findMode`, Loop's
      abbreviation of `loopHostM body F anchor false findMode` (round-1 bridge probe: `rfl`);
    - `f2_loopHost_prepare … ↦ loopHost_prepare … false …`, and the same for `_start`;
    - every other `f2_X ↦ X`; `f2_head_steps` ↦ the stand-in through `Finset.mem_Icc.mp`;
    - the coefficient made explicit (below).

    No `f2_` or `a2_` token remains anywhere in the overlay (asserted by the builder).
- **Part 2** (525 lines) is the unit's Loop part (unit lines 799–1488):
  - its three gate-shim blocks are dropped (the overlay has the originals);
  - two docstrings no longer name `f2_` declarations (`part2-vs-unit.diff`);
  - **every `sorry` is replaced by a proof** over the declarations of part 1:
    - `loopHostTM_contracts`: the moved `loopHost_contracts`, its two head clauses dropped;
    - `loopHostTM_decides`, `loopHostTM_finds`: the bodies of `exists_loopTM` and
      `exists_loopFindTM` over the named host, with `c = 10`;
    - `loopHostTM_spaceUsed_le_budget`: the moved contract and `seamed_space` (the spec
      probe's glue, now relative to the real declarations);
    - `emitLoopTM_computes`: the tip's `exists_emitLoopTM` body, extracted, the host named;
    - `callTM_run`: `emCall_first`.

The overlay imports exactly `Loop.lean`'s six imports and `TuringMachine.Simulation` (the unit
Loop part's one extra `@imports`, already in Loop's closure). It does not import `Loop`. Being a
full copy of `Loop`, it is elaborated in Loop's import closure: the cut-check method.

**The explicit coefficient (a private statement change).** Catalog's contract states
`∃ c : ℕ, ∀ x, …` and opens its proof with `refine ⟨f2_loopHost_bound, ?_⟩`. The public
`loopHostTM_contracts` names `10`, which an `∃ c` statement cannot supply. So the moved
contract takes the transform that round 1's manifest applies to `loopHostTM_contracts` and to
its probe shim `loopHost_contracts_heads`: `∃ c` removed, `c ↦ 10`, the `refine` line deleted.
`loopHost_bound` reduces to `10`; the proof's internal bounds still use it.

## Decisions in force (verify that the files reflect them)

**User decisions of 2026-10-13, binding** (MIG1-design §14):
- **M1, first form.** The B5a continuations are integrated and no B5a worker is active, so MIG-1
  retires all six R3 canonical `_run` rows, including `copyTM_run`'s consumer edit at
  `CodeSimulator.lean:1295`, in its last PR. That edit is sequenced with the H2-M move, which
  also edits `CodeSimulator.lean` (PR sequence below).
- **M2.** Both consolidations: `computesFunInTime_pairDup` onto Encoding's `Turing.pairDiagTM`;
  `computesFunInTime_pairMapSnd` onto the forwarding controller of its own space row, retiring
  `pairMapTM`.
- **M3.** The 20 Catalog space rows stay in Catalog as corollaries; only witness-intrinsic proofs
  move; Catalog imports Primitives (no cycle: Primitives does not import Catalog, measured).
- **M4.** MIG-17's "named loop hosts" item is done by MIG-1 (`loopHostTM`, `emitLoopTM`,
  `callTM`); MIG-17 keeps the Contract rebase of the loop hosts and `splitSafe`/`SafeRun`.
- **Style.** Spec theorems in the existing style, not `Contract` instances. The decision is
  binding; its rationale, restated accurately (design §2): **reason 2, shape** — 28 of the 34
  home rows are whole-machine computations from `initCfg` to a halt, judged by the output, and
  today's proofs fix neither an exact halting time nor the endpoint's work tapes, so a
  `Contract` instance would carry `post := runFrom … time` and add no content; the space rows
  bound `spaceUsed` from `initCfg` at every time, not inside an interval envelope. **Reason 3,
  order** — a `Contract M …` needs a named `M`, so named witnesses are a prerequisite of MIG-11
  and MIG-17, not an alternative. **Reason 1, layering, is temporary**: it holds for
  `Build/Contract.lean` as landed today (it imports Catalog), but MIG-0b's round-2 draft splits
  it into a core `Build/Contract/Basic`, whose closure is `Configuration`, `Deterministic`,
  `Finite`, `Simulation`, `StateRenaming` (MIG-0b round-2 `NOTES-r2.md` §3 and §10 item 6, not
  yet in the repository; `BUNDLE-MISSING.txt`), plus
  `Contract/Seam`, `/Embed`, `/Catalog`, `/Lift` and a facade. After that split every MIG-1 home
  except Simulation could import the core; the decision does not rest on layering.

**Earlier rulings**: design §2, the named-witness rule (constructive layers export named machines
with spec theorems; existential packaging only at the consumer layer); §16 decision 1 (byte
identity of §8 and the byte-identical `Primitives` of 12.2 lifted) and decision 2, scenario B
(retire the R3 canonical rows with their consumers edited); user rule: file size alone is never a
reason to split.

**Why one unit.** A file elaborated against the snapshot can import only existing modules, and
later parts use earlier parts' declarations. Each part's cut file is the copyright block, the
part's imports (the existing home module and the modules it imports that carry parts), the
standard options, and the bodies of the parts in its closure (`scripts/cutcheck.py`, the stage-2
gate's script, unchanged).

**Landing is a set of edits, not a cut.** (1) A witness that is today a private definition of its
home lands *in place*: `private` goes, the name changes by the rename map, the body is
unchanged, the docstring becomes the unit's; every other occurrence in the home file is renamed
by the same asserted script. Rename map (`scripts/renames.json`): `catalogPrefixTM → prependTM`,
`emitterTokenTM → unaryTokenTM`, `emitterAppendTM → appendBitTM`, `loopHost → loopHostTM`,
`emCallTM → callTM`, `Complexity.counterTM → Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM` (declared with
`_root_.`; the file's private lemmas then say `FinTM.lengthBitsTM` under `open Turing`), and the
four promotions `catalogPrefixTM_computes → prependTM_computes`, `pairExtract_computes →
pairExtractTM_computes`, `pairValid_computes → pairValidTM_computes`, `incFixed_computes →
incFixedTM_computes`. (2) The **gate shims** (between `-- @shim begin` and `-- @shim end`) are
verbatim copies of the private definitions a witness body uses; they exist only because private
declarations of another module cannot be named, and are dropped on landing. (3) New definitions
and specs are inserted before the first row they serve. (4) The `MIG1Gate.*` declarations are not
landed; at the fill stage each row's proof becomes its `MIG1Gate.row_*` proof.

## What the files state (verify)

Constants are explicit. "S1" marks a promoted private lemma (statement verbatim modulo the
rename), "S3" a statement verbatim from a proved Catalog lemma that moves, "probe" a spec that the
spec probe derives from verbatim statements of proved private lemmas, "proved" a spec proved in
the unit.

**Part 1, Simulation.** `abs_workTapePos_runFrom_sub_le M d t j : |(M.runFrom d t).workTapePos j -
d.workTapePos j| ≤ t` (proved; H2's statement and proof). `ComputesInTime.spaceUsed_le (h :
M.ComputesInTime x y T) t : M.tm.spaceUsed (M.tm.initCfg x) t ≤ M.k * (T + 1)` (proved;
`f2_space_of_time`). `branchTM_spaceUsed M₁ M₂ b x t : (branchTM M₁ M₂ b).tm.spaceUsed … t = if b
then M₁…spaceUsed … t + M₂.k else M₂…spaceUsed … t + M₁.k` (S3, `f2_branch_space`).

**Part 2, Composition.** `idTM` (0 tapes, copies the input), `constTM w` (0 tapes, emits `w`),
`ifEqTM w₀ u v` (0 tapes, compares with `w₀`, emits `u` or `v`), `condTM D M₁ M₂` (register
conditional). `idTM_computes x : idTM.ComputesInTime x x (|x| + 1)` (probe);
`constTM_computes w x : (constTM w).ComputesInTime x w (|w| + 1)` (proved);
`ifEqTM_computes : ComputesFunInTime (if · = w₀ then u else v) ((|w₀| + max |u| |v| + 3)(n + 1))`
(probe); `bufferedCompTM_computesFunInTime (h₁ h₂ hT₂) : (bufferedCompTM M₁ M₂).ComputesFunInTime
(g ∘ f) (2(T₁ n + T₂ (T₁ n) + 1))`, `bufferedCompTM_computesFunInTime_on_image : … g (2T₁ n + T₂ n
+ 2)`, `bufferedCompTM_computes_iff M₁ M₂ x w` (the halting relation of `exists_comp_partial`)
(all proved, the rows' bodies); `condTM_computes_iff (hD : D.Computes [p ·]) x w : (∃ t,
condTM… x w t) ↔ ∃ t, (cond (p x) M₁ M₂)… x w t` (probe).

**Part 3, Wrappers.** `timedCondTM D M₁ M₂` (captured decider, verdict read, rewind, branch
bank). `timedCondTM_computes (hD h₁ h₂) : … (if p x then f₁ x else f₂ x) (5(T₀ n + max (T₁ n)
(T₂ n) + 1))` (S3, `f2_cond_time`, the row's body); `timedCondTM_spaceUsed D M₁ M₂ x b T t (hD :
D.ComputesInTime x [b] T) : space ≤ D's space at T + branch space at t + 2` (S3,
`f2_cond_space`); `redirectTM_runFrom M haltOn x t`: the redirected run's state (the source state
with the last emitted bit while live; after the halt, halted iff that bit is `haltOn`, else the
live loop), input position, work tapes and heads equal the source run's, output `[]` (probe; the
public field form of the private `redirect_run`).

**Part 4, Encoding.** `Turing.pairDiagTM` (six states, 0 tapes, outputs `pairEncode α α`);
`pairDiagTM_computes x : … (pairEncode x x) (4|x| + 5)` (probe). `FinTM.toCodeTM : (M : FinTM
Bool) → M.k = 1 → CodeTM` (noncomputable; `⟨|Q| − 1, tm.relabelState e⟩` with `e =
Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq`); `toCodeTM_computesInTime_iff M hk x o t` (proved).

**Part 5, TimeConstructible.** `Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM` (one tape, four states, the binary
counter). `lengthBitsTM_computes : ComputesFunInTime (Nat.bits |x|) (5(n + 1))` (S3,
`f2_counter_computes`, the `timeConstructible_id` body); `lengthBitsTM_spaceUsed x t : space ≤
5(Nat.size |x| + 1)` (S3, `f2_counter_space`).

**Part 6, Loop.** `loopHostTM body F anchor findMode := loopHostM body F anchor false findMode`
(abbreviation, as today); `emitLoopTM body F anchor := emLoopHost body F anchor true` (the
forwarding host in find mode); `callTM M emit` (today `emCallTM`), `callEntry M emit :=
(callTM M emit).tm.q₀`, `callExit M emit := .inr (.inr 5)`. `loopHostTM_contracts` (today's

`emitLoopTM_computes` (`10(T n + 1)(R n + 2)`, the row's body); `callTM_k_pos` (proved);
`callTM_run M emit x arg cap T (hM : M.ComputesInTime arg cap T) : ∃ t ≤ (24 + 13·k_M)(T + |arg|
+ |cap| + 1), 0 < t ∧ (∀ j < t, state ≠ some (callExit M emit)) ∧ runFrom … t = {ofWords
(callExit M emit) (stateWord k (if emit then arg else cap)) with output := if emit then cap else

**Part 7, Primitives.** S1: `prependTM_computes w : ComputesFunInTime (w ++ ·) (|w| + n + 1)`,

↦ constTM (replicate C true)`, `d + 1 ↦` the private engine); `polyUnaryTM_computes C e : …

## Changes from the draft and the design (and why)

1. **Every witness has its real body** (the draft left `loopHostTM`, `callTM`, `callEntry`,
   `callExit`, `pairMapSndTM` and an engine `sorry`), checked against its source.
2. **Landing names directly** (draft: namespace `MIG1Draft`): a private declaration's name is
   module-local, so the public names can be declared against the snapshot; only the rows need
   gate names (`MIG1Gate.row_*`).
3. **The run-form head lemma is H2's** `abs_workTapePos_runFrom_sub_le` (design:
   `workTapePos_runFrom_le`), so that MIG-1 and H2 share one lemma; MIG-0b's interval form may
   make it a corollary (PR sequence, open question 3).
4. **`ComputesInTime.spaceUsed_le` is homed in Simulation** (design: Catalog): it is generic, and
   the moved space proofs and later Primitives space specs can then use it.
5. **The `_k` lemmas are dropped**: `rfl` gives every tape count; no consumer needs a name.
6. **`polyUnaryTM_computes` is sharp**: `(C + 5e + 4)(n + 1)^e`, without the draft's linear
   allowance, which only `f2_unary_sharp`'s reuse of the constant row's existential constant
   needed; there is no `polyUnaryEngineTM`, the engine stays the private `catalogPolyUnaryTM`.
7. **One clean-call contract** `callTM_run` for both modes, with today's full first-exit cut
   `∀ j < t` (design: `callTM_install`, `callTM_emit`, positive-only cut); the rows weaken it.
8. **The loop's space** is `loopHostTM_spaceUsed_le_budget` (both modes, time hypotheses only,
   `23·k·(T + 1)`), replacing the draft's decision-mode `loopHostTM_spaceUsed` (`19·k·(S + T +
   1)`, with fuel and body space hypotheses); `exists_loopTM_spaceUsed` is its corollary
   (open question 1).
9. **`redirectTM_runFrom` is stated field by field**, so that no private definition occurs in a
   public statement.
10. **`pairMapSndTM` lands at F-B**, not S: its body is Catalog's private controller, which can
    move to Primitives only together with its 24 lemmas.
11. **`splitSolveWithTM E` takes only the width machine**: the width function does not occur in
    the machine (design signature `(ℕ → ℕ) → FinTM Bool → FinTM Bool`).
12. **`polyBitsTM`** follows today's space proof's case split exactly (`constTM (Nat.bits 0)` at
    `C = 0`), and its time spec is proved here with the constant `7C + 5e + 11` at degree `e`
    (design ESTIMATE: degree `e + 1`).
13. **The composite constants are checked by Lean** (spec probe), not estimated: `150`,
    `C + 5e + 17`, `20((C + 1 + 5e)2^e + 46)`, `20(591 + 26·k_E)`, `23·k`.
14. **The R3 retirement uses two endpoint lemmas** (design §7), proved here; each retired row is
    re-derived from them in four lines (`MIG1Gate.retired_*`), which is the consumer edit.
15. **The deletion plan** has new fates: seven duplicates of public lemmas, the 14-lemma `a2_`
    ledger deleted with the S-form, the split originals kept (above).

## PR sequence and batching (design §8–§10, updated)

**Bold alert: H2-M and MIG-1 share `CodeSimulator.lean` and one lemma; land H2-M first.**

0. **H2-M** (maintainer; already scheduled for the coordinated window before the next B5a brief,

   lines 2869–4466) to `Build/StepBlock.lean`, including `abs_workTapePos_runFrom_sub_le`.

**MIG-0b and MIG-1: neither must land first.** MIG-1 uses no contract (style decision) and
MIG-0b uses no MIG-1 declaration; MIG-17 needs both. Either order keeps the import graph acyclic
(MIG-0b's core imports nothing above Simulation; Catalog's new Primitives import only enlarges
`Contract/Catalog`'s closure). The interactions are textual and one shared fact (MIG-0b's
landing set, `r2-mig0b/landing/`, MEASURED):

  region and the R3 rows (F-D). The edits are disjoint, no region declaration cites that lemma
  (inventory §2.1, re-checked), and the deletion plan is keyed by name, so the later PR rebases

## Brief for the auditor

Restate every definition in your own words before reading its docstring; argue each sorried
theorem true in 2–5 sentences or exhibit a counterexample; attempt at least six adversarial

"""MIG-24 triage, read-only: for each candidate pair, extract both declarations and compare tokens.
rename-mirror: equal up to a consistent renaming of identifiers; variant: otherwise (equal-token %)."""
import re, sys, os, difflib, csv
root, cand, pop, out = sys.argv[1:5]
src = open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), 'declfreeze_chunks.py')).read()
ns = {}; exec(src, ns); chunks = ns['chunks']
paths = [l.strip() for l in open(pop) if l.strip()]
def resolve(f):
    if os.path.exists(os.path.join(root, f)): return f
    hits = [p for p in paths if p.endswith('/' + f)]
    return hits[0] if len(hits) == 1 else None
cache = {}
def decl(f, n):
    p = resolve(f)
    if p is None: return None, 'unresolved file'
    if p not in cache:
        cache[p] = {name: t for name, _, t in chunks(open(os.path.join(root, p), encoding='utf-8').read())}
    t = cache[p].get(n)
    return (p, t) if t else (p, None)
TOK = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_'.₀-₉ᵢ]*|\d+|\S")
def toks(t):
    body = t.split('-/', 1)[1] if t.lstrip().startswith('/--') else t
    body = re.sub(r'--[^\n]*', '', body)
    return TOK.findall(body)
rows = []
for r in csv.DictReader(open(cand, encoding='utf-8'), delimiter='\t'):
    pa, ta = decl(r['file_a'], r['decl_a']); pb, tb = decl(r['file_b'], r['decl_b'])
    if not ta or not tb:
        rows.append({**r, 'class': 'unresolved', 'equal_pct': '', 'renames': '', 'path_a': pa or '', 'path_b': pb or ''}); continue
    A, B = toks(ta), toks(tb)
    sm = difflib.SequenceMatcher(a=A, b=B, autojunk=False)
    eq = sum(bl.size for bl in sm.get_matching_blocks())
    pct = round(100 * eq / max(len(A), len(B)))
    mapping, ok = {}, True
    for tag, i1, i2, j1, j2 in sm.get_opcodes():
        if tag == 'equal': continue
        if tag != 'replace' or i2 - i1 != j2 - j1: ok = False; break
        for x, y in zip(A[i1:i2], B[j1:j2]):
            if not (re.match(r'[A-Za-z_]', x) and re.match(r'[A-Za-z_]', y)): ok = False; break
            if mapping.setdefault(x, y) != y: ok = False; break
        if not ok: break
    cls = 'rename-mirror' if ok else 'variant'
    rows.append({**r, 'class': cls, 'equal_pct': pct, 'renames': ' '.join(f'{a}->{b}' for a, b in list(mapping.items())[:8]) if ok else '',
                 'path_a': pa, 'path_b': pb})
keys = list(rows[0].keys())
with open(out, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=keys, delimiter='\t'); w.writeheader(); w.writerows(rows)
from collections import Counter
print(Counter(r['class'] for r in rows))

## ===== campaign/items/mig24/overnight.sh =====

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The overnight screens, one at a time, at #118's round-2 head (wt-bapi, 4624fc05), after any running
# screen: the F3 and cont6 screen bases re-measured (their populations contain round-2 files),
# then MIG-24's library-wide screens of TuringMachine/ and SpaceComplexity/.
S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-seyoonr-phd-experiments-tcslib/8f0076bc-454a-4666-b8cf-f4c7ed13c549/scratchpad
N=$S/mig24
busy() { pgrep -f 'Python -I audits/evidence/retrofit/[c]opy-text-screen-v3' >/dev/null; }
run() {  # name, population file, output
  while busy; do sleep 30; done
  echo "$(date +%H:%M) start $1" >> "$N/overnight.log"
  nice -n 10 python3 -I audits/evidence/retrofit/copy-text-screen-v3.py . $(grep -v '^#' "$2") > "$3" 2>&1
  echo "$(date +%H:%M) $1: $(sed -n 1p "$3")" >> "$N/overnight.log"
}
cd "$S/wt-bapi" || exit 1
run f3-r2 "$S/issue5/f3-pop.txt" "$S/issue5/f3-screen-base-r2.txt"
run c6-r2 "$S/issue5/c6-pop.txt" "$S/issue5/c6-screen-base-r2.txt"
for b in tm sc; do
  run "mig24-$b" "$N/pop-$b.txt" "$N/screen-$b.txt"
  python3 -I - "$N/screen-$b.txt" "$N/pairs90-$b.txt" <<'PY'
import sys, re
rows = [l.rstrip('\n') for l in open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8') if (m := re.search(r'= (\d+)%$', l.rstrip())) and int(m.group(1)) >= 90]
open(sys.argv[2], 'w', encoding='utf-8').write('\n'.join(rows) + '\n')
PY
  echo "$(date +%H:%M) mig24-$b pairs at 90% or more: $(grep -c . "$N/pairs90-$b.txt")" >> "$N/overnight.log"
done
cat "$N/overnight.log"

import Mathlib.Order.Monotone.Defs
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Sum
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Prod
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Option
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Simulation

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Composition of Turing machine computations

Basic computability combinators for the bundled machines: the identity and constant
functions are linear-time computable, and time-bounded computability is closed under
composition. Composition is the load-bearing lemma of the whole development — the
universal machine (phase 3) and the `HALT` reduction (phase 4) are built from it — and
it is the part [AB09] never spells out, dispatching it with "high-level descriptions"
of machines. The Isabelle AFP `Cook_Levin` entry spends a large fraction of its effort
exactly here.

## Design

Composition is stated at the *specification* level (`ComputesFunInTime`), not as an
operator on raw machines: the composed machine is existentially produced. Internally
(proof obligation, not API) the construction simulates `M₁` with its emissions
redirected to a fresh work tape, then simulates `M₂` reading that tape in place of its
input tape.

**Convention obligation status** (phase-1 audit finding 4; phase-2 audit finding 3):
this file does *not* formally discharge the append-only vs read-write output-tape
bridge. Every statement here — hypotheses and conclusions alike — lives in the
append-only model, and [AB09]'s read-write-output machine is not formalized in this
development, so no simulation between the two conventions can even be stated yet. The
obligation is recorded in the plan's decision log as **waived**, with the compensating
restriction that no exact-step-count transfer from [AB09] is ever claimed: every bound
*adapted from the source* carries an existential constant (purely internal results,
such as the oracle lockstep lemmas, are legitimately exact but never cross a
convention), and every result is self-contained in-model. A formal bridge (a
read-write-output machine variant plus a simulation theorem) will be added if and only
if a downstream result needs it. What this file *does* provide is the buffer-and-flush
technique — an emission can be deferred to a work tape and flushed at the end — which
is what delayed or revisable output looks like *within this model*; whether the
append-only convention matches [AB09]'s read-write one remains formally unestablished,
per the waiver.

The generic simulation gadgets this file's machines are assembled from — emission
chains, control actions, disjoint tape-block embeddings with their lockstep run
lemmas, the input-head rewind, and the two-machine branch union — live in
`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Simulation` (split out at the epoch-1/epoch-2
boundary, per the epoch-1 audit findings 5 and 11 and the policy file-size
standard); this file keeps only its concrete machines and their theorems.

## Main definitions

The named witnesses of the combinators below (MIG-1): `Turing.FinTM.idTM` (copy),
`Turing.FinTM.constTM` (constant), `Turing.FinTM.ifEqTM` (fixed-word comparator) and
`Turing.FinTM.condTM` (untimed conditional); the composite is
`Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM` of `TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Simulation`.

## Main results

* The witnesses' specs (MIG-1): `Turing.FinTM.idTM_computes`,
  `Turing.FinTM.constTM_computes`, `Turing.FinTM.ifEqTM_computes`,
  `Turing.FinTM.condTM_computes_iff`, and the buffered composition's
  `Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM_computesFunInTime`,
  `Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM_computesFunInTime_on_image` and
  `Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM_computes_iff`. `idTM_computes`, `ifEqTM_computes` and
  `condTM_computes_iff` are sorried until the fill F-A; the others are proved.
* Time-bounded combinators (all over the binary alphabet):
  `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_id`, `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_const`,
  `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_ifEq`, `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_comp`.
* **Partial (guarded) combinators** — the phase-4 API mandated by the phase-3 audit
  (round 2, finding 10 and Argument F: the total-function composition cannot take
  the partially computing universal evaluator as a component):
  `Turing.FinTM.exists_comp_partial` composes two arbitrary machines at the level of
  their halting relations, with the intermediate output buffered on a work tape;
  `Turing.FinTM.exists_cond` branches between two machines on a decided predicate.
  Both are stated untimed; the forward time bound of the buffered composition is
  `Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM_computesInTime`, and `Turing.FinTM.exists_comp_on_image`
  composes with a second machine that is correct only on the first one's image.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.2-§1.3; the "high-level description"
  convention on p. 14.)
* [Balbach22] F. J. Balbach, *The Cook-Levin theorem*, Archive of Formal Proofs
  (Isabelle), 2022 — the composition-combinator architecture this file follows in
  spirit.
-/

namespace Turing.FinTM

/-- **The copy machine**. A machine with no work tapes and one state that writes each input symbol
to its output while moving right, and halts on the blank after the input. [AB09, §1.2] -/
def idTM : FinTM Bool where
  k := 0
  State := Unit
  tm :=
    { q₀ := ()
      tr := fun _ inp _ =>
        match inp with
        | some b => ⟨SignType.pos, fun i => i.elim0, some b, some ()⟩
        | none => ⟨SignType.zero, fun i => i.elim0, none, none⟩ }

/-- Run invariant of the copy machine: after `t ≤ n` steps it is live, its input head
sits at position `t + 1`, and it has emitted exactly the first `t` input bits. -/
private lemma idTM_run (x : List Bool) : ∀ t, t ≤ x.length →
    (idTM.tm.runFrom (idTM.tm.initCfg x) t).state = some () ∧
    (((idTM.tm.runFrom (idTM.tm.initCfg x) t).inputPos : ℕ) = t + 1) ∧
    (idTM.tm.runFrom (idTM.tm.initCfg x) t).output = x.take t := by
  intro t
  induction t with
  | zero =>
    intro _
    refine ⟨rfl, ?_, rfl⟩
    simp [MultiTapeTM.runFrom]
  | succ t ih =>
    intro ht
    obtain ⟨hstate, hpos, hout⟩ := ih (Nat.le_of_succ_le ht)
    have hrun1 : idTM.tm.runFrom (idTM.tm.initCfg x) (t + 1) =
        (idTM.tm.tr () (some (x[t]'(by omega)))
          ((idTM.tm.runFrom (idTM.tm.initCfg x) t).workTapeSymbols)).apply
          (idTM.tm.runFrom (idTM.tm.initCfg x) t) := by
      rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step']
      unfold MultiTapeTM.step
      rw [hstate]
      dsimp only
      rw [inputSymbolInner (p := t) (by omega) (by omega)]
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [hrun1]
      simp [idTM, Action.apply]
    · rw [hrun1]
      simp only [idTM, Action.apply]
      rw [moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right _ (by omega)]
      show ((idTM.tm.runFrom (idTM.tm.initCfg x) t).inputPos : ℕ) + 1 = t + 2
      omega
    · rw [hrun1]
      simp only [idTM, Action.apply]
      rw [hout, List.take_succ, List.getElem?_eq_getElem (by omega)]

/-- **The copy machine's time**. On every input `x` the copy machine halts within `|x| + 1` steps
with output `x`. [AB09, §1.2]

**Proof sketch.** The body of today's `computesFunInTime_id` up to its final weakening: by the
private run invariant `idTM_run`, after `|x|` steps the machine is live, its input head is at cell
`|x| + 1` and it has written `x`; there it reads the blank, and the next step halts without writing.
-/
theorem idTM_computes (x : List Bool) : idTM.ComputesInTime x x (x.length + 1) := by
  sorry

/-- The identity function is computable in linear time: the copy machine halts within
`n + 1` steps having emitted its input verbatim (invariant `idTM_run`, then one
halting step on the boundary blank). -/
theorem computesFunInTime_id :
    ∃ (M : FinTM Bool) (c : ℕ), M.ComputesFunInTime id fun n => c * (n + 1) := by
  refine ⟨idTM, 1, fun x => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨hstate, hpos, hout⟩ := idTM_run x x.length (le_refl _)
  have h0 : (idTM.tm.runFrom (idTM.tm.initCfg x) x.length).inputPos ≠ 0 := by
    intro h
    rw [h] at hpos
    simp at hpos
  have hsym : (idTM.tm.runFrom (idTM.tm.initCfg x) x.length).inputSymbol = none := by
    unfold Cfg.inputSymbol
    rw [dif_neg h0, dif_pos (by omega)]
  have hrun1 : idTM.tm.runFrom (idTM.tm.initCfg x) (x.length + 1) =
      (idTM.tm.tr () none
        ((idTM.tm.runFrom (idTM.tm.initCfg x) x.length).workTapeSymbols)).apply
        (idTM.tm.runFrom (idTM.tm.initCfg x) x.length) := by
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step']
    unfold MultiTapeTM.step
    rw [hstate]
    dsimp only
    rw [hsym]
  have hbase : idTM.ComputesInTime x x (x.length + 1) := by
    refine ⟨_, ?_, ?_, rfl⟩
    · rw [hrun1]
      simp [idTM, Action.apply]
    · rw [hrun1]
      simp only [idTM, Action.apply]
      rw [hout]
      simp
  exact hbase.mono (le_of_eq (one_mul _).symm)

/-- **The constant machine**. A machine with no work tapes whose `|w| + 1` states form the emission
chain of the fixed word `w`: it writes `w`, one symbol per step, ignoring its input, and halts.
[AB09, §1.2] -/
def constTM (w : List Bool) : FinTM Bool where
  k := 0
  State := Fin (w.length + 1)
  tm := { q₀ := 0, tr := fun i _ _ => emitAction w id i }

/-- **The constant machine's time**. On every input the constant machine halts within `|w| + 1`
steps with output `w`. [AB09, §1.2]

**Proof sketch.** The emission chain writes `w` in `|w|` steps and halts on the next
(`Turing.FinTM.emit_halts`), appending to the initially empty output. -/
theorem constTM_computes (w x : List Bool) :
    (constTM w).ComputesInTime x w (w.length + 1) := by
  obtain ⟨hs, ho⟩ := emit_halts (constTM w).tm w id (fun _ _ _ => rfl)
    ((constTM w).tm.initCfg x) rfl
  exact ⟨_, hs, by simpa only [MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init, List.nil_append] using ho, rfl⟩

/-- Every constant function is computable in linear time (in fact in time `|w| + 1`,
which the stated bound dominates once `c ≥ |w| + 1`).

**Proof sketch.** A zero-work-tape machine with `|w| + 1` states `s₀, …, s_{|w|}`:
state `sᵢ` emits the `i`-th symbol of `w` and moves to `s_{i+1}`, ignoring the input;
`s_{|w|}` halts. -/
theorem computesFunInTime_const (w : List Bool) :
    ∃ (M : FinTM Bool) (c : ℕ), M.ComputesFunInTime (fun _ => w) fun n => c * (n + 1) := by
  refine ⟨constTM w, w.length + 1, fun x => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨hs, ho⟩ := emit_halts (constTM w).tm w id (fun _ _ _ => rfl)
    ((constTM w).tm.initCfg x) rfl
  have hbase : (constTM w).ComputesInTime x w (w.length + 1) := by
    exact ⟨_, hs, by simpa only [MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init, List.nil_append] using ho, rfl⟩
  exact hbase.mono (Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (by omega))

/-- **The fixed-word comparator**. A machine with no work tapes that compares its input with the
fixed word `w₀` symbol by symbol and then runs the emission chain of `u` (on an exact match followed
by the blank) or of `v` (on the first mismatch, an early blank, or a symbol past the end of `w₀`).
[AB09, §1.2] -/
def ifEqTM (w₀ u v : List Bool) : FinTM Bool where
  k := 0
  State := Fin (w₀.length + 1) ⊕ (Fin (u.length + 1) ⊕ Fin (v.length + 1))
  tm :=
    { q₀ := .inl 0
      tr := fun q inp _ => match q with
        | .inl i =>
          if h : i.val < w₀.length then
            if inp = some w₀[i.val] then
              controlAction .pos (some (.inl ⟨i.val + 1, by omega⟩))
            else controlAction 0 (some (.inr (.inr 0)))
          else if inp = none then controlAction 0 (some (.inr (.inl 0)))
            else controlAction 0 (some (.inr (.inr 0)))
        | .inr (.inl i) => emitAction u (fun j => .inr (.inl j)) i
        | .inr (.inr i) => emitAction v (fun j => .inr (.inr j)) i }

/-- Once the comparator has chosen its output chain, that chain emits the selected
word and halts, independently of the input-head position. -/
private lemma ifEq_finish (w₀ u v x : List Bool) (b : Bool)
    (cfg : Cfg 0 Bool (ifEqTM w₀ u v).State x)
    (hs : cfg.state = some (.inr (cond b (.inl 0) (.inr 0)))) (ho : cfg.output = []) :
    ((ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm.runFrom cfg ((cond b u v).length + 1)).state = none ∧
    ((ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm.runFrom cfg ((cond b u v).length + 1)).output = cond b u v := by
  cases b
  · simpa only [Bool.cond_false, ho, List.nil_append] using
      emit_halts (ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm v (fun j => .inr (.inr j))
        (fun _ _ _ => rfl) cfg hs
  · simpa only [Bool.cond_true, ho, List.nil_append] using
      emit_halts (ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm u (fun j => .inr (.inl j))
        (fun _ _ _ => rfl) cfg hs

/-- Comparison invariant: the first `i` symbols match, and the head is at `i + 1`.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on the number of remaining comparison symbols. A matching
symbol advances the invariant. A mismatch selects the second emission chain. With
no symbols remaining, the boundary blank selects the first chain and an extra
symbol selects the second. The emission-chain lemma supplies the remaining time. -/
private lemma ifEq_run (w₀ u v x : List Bool) : ∀ (r i : ℕ) (hlen : w₀.length = i + r), i ≤ x.length → x.take i = w₀.take i →
    ∀ (cfg : Cfg 0 Bool (ifEqTM w₀ u v).State x),
      cfg.state = some (.inl ⟨i, by omega⟩) → cfg.inputPos.val = i + 1 → cfg.output = [] →
      ∃ t, t ≤ r + max u.length v.length + 2 ∧
        ((ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm.runFrom cfg t).state = none ∧
        ((ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm.runFrom cfg t).output = if x = w₀ then u else v := by
  intro r
  induction r with
  | zero =>
    intro i hlen hix hprefix cfg hs hp ho
    have hi : ¬i < w₀.length := by omega
    have hsym := inputSymbol_at cfg i hix hp
    by_cases he : x = w₀
    · subst x
      have hb : w₀[i]? = none := List.getElem?_eq_none_iff.mpr (by omega)
      have hstep : (ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm.step cfg =
          (controlAction 0 (some (.inr (.inl 0)))).apply cfg := by
        unfold MultiTapeTM.step
        rw [hs]
        simp only [ifEqTM, hsym, dif_neg hi, hb, ite_true]
      have hs' : ((ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm.step cfg).state = some (.inr (.inl 0)) := by
        rw [hstep]
        rfl
      have ho' : ((ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm.step cfg).output = [] := by
        simp [hstep, controlAction, Action.apply, ho]
      have hf := ifEq_finish w₀ u v w₀ true _ hs' ho'
      refine ⟨u.length + 1 + 1, by omega, ?_⟩
      rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step]
      simpa only [Bool.cond_true, if_pos rfl] using hf
    · have hx : i < x.length := by
        by_contra hh
        have hxt : x.take i = x := List.take_of_length_le (by omega)
        have hwt : w₀.take i = w₀ := List.take_of_length_le (by omega)
        exact he (by rw [← hxt, ← hwt]; exact hprefix)
      have hb : x[i]? = some x[i] := List.getElem?_eq_getElem hx
      have hstep : (ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm.step cfg =
          (controlAction 0 (some (.inr (.inr 0)))).apply cfg := by
        unfold MultiTapeTM.step
        rw [hs]
        simp only [ifEqTM, hsym, dif_neg hi, hb, Option.some_ne_none, ite_false]
      have hs' : ((ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm.step cfg).state = some (.inr (.inr 0)) := by
        rw [hstep]
        rfl
      have ho' : ((ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm.step cfg).output = [] := by
        simp [hstep, controlAction, Action.apply, ho]
      have hf := ifEq_finish w₀ u v x false _ hs' ho'
      refine ⟨v.length + 1 + 1, by omega, ?_⟩
      rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step]
      simpa only [Bool.cond_false, if_neg he] using hf
  | succ r ih =>
    intro i hlen hix hprefix cfg hs hp ho
    have hi : i < w₀.length := by omega
    have hsym := inputSymbol_at cfg i hix hp
    by_cases hm : x[i]? = some w₀[i]
    · obtain ⟨hx, hbit⟩ := List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.mp hm
      have hstep : (ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm.step cfg =
          (controlAction .pos (some (.inl ⟨i + 1, by omega⟩))).apply cfg := by
        unfold MultiTapeTM.step
        rw [hs]
        simp only [ifEqTM, hsym, dif_pos hi, hm, ite_true]
      have hs' : ((ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm.step cfg).state =
          some (.inl ⟨i + 1, by omega⟩) := by rw [hstep]; rfl
      have hp' : ((ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm.step cfg).inputPos.val = (i + 1) + 1 := by
        rw [hstep]
        change (moveInputPos cfg.inputPos .pos).val = i + 1 + 1
        rw [moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right _ (by omega)]
        simp only
        omega
      have ho' : ((ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm.step cfg).output = [] := by
        simp [hstep, controlAction, Action.apply, ho]
      have hprefix' : x.take (i + 1) = w₀.take (i + 1) := by
        rw [List.take_succ, List.take_succ, hprefix, hm, List.getElem?_eq_getElem hi]
      obtain ⟨t, ht, htstate, htout⟩ := ih (i + 1) (by omega) (by omega) hprefix'
        ((ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm.step cfg) hs' hp' ho'
      refine ⟨t + 1, by omega, ?_⟩
      rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step]
      exact ⟨htstate, htout⟩
    · have he : x ≠ w₀ := by
        intro he
        subst x
        exact hm (List.getElem?_eq_getElem hi)
      have hstep : (ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm.step cfg =
          (controlAction 0 (some (.inr (.inr 0)))).apply cfg := by
        unfold MultiTapeTM.step
        rw [hs]
        simp only [ifEqTM, hsym, dif_pos hi, if_neg hm]
      have hs' : ((ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm.step cfg).state = some (.inr (.inr 0)) := by
        rw [hstep]
        rfl
      have ho' : ((ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm.step cfg).output = [] := by
        simp [hstep, controlAction, Action.apply, ho]
      have hf := ifEq_finish w₀ u v x false _ hs' ho'
      refine ⟨v.length + 1 + 1, by omega, ?_⟩
      rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step]
      simpa only [Bool.cond_false, if_neg he] using hf

/-- **The comparator's time**. The comparator computes `w ↦ if w = w₀ then u else v` within
`(|w₀| + max |u| |v| + 3)·(n + 1)` steps, the constant of today's row made explicit.

**Proof sketch.** The body of today's `computesFunInTime_ifEq`: the private comparison run
`ifEq_run` reaches the halt within `|w₀| + max |u| |v| + 3` steps with the selected word as output,
and that constant is at most its product with `n + 1`. -/
theorem ifEqTM_computes (w₀ u v : List Bool) :
    (ifEqTM w₀ u v).ComputesFunInTime (fun w => if w = w₀ then u else v)
      (fun n => (w₀.length + max u.length v.length + 3) * (n + 1)) := by
  sorry

/-- Testing equality with a fixed string is computable in linear time: for any fixed
`w₀ u v`, the function `w ↦ u` if `w = w₀` and `w ↦ v` otherwise. (Instantiated by
the `HALT` reduction as the postprocessor `w ↦ if w = [true] then [false] else
[true]`; see `TCSlib.Complexity.Uncomputability.Halting`.)

**Proof sketch.** Hardcode `w₀`, `u`, and `v` in the states. The machine walks the
input left to right comparing it against `w₀` symbol by symbol (`|w₀| + 1`
comparison states); on the first mismatch — including the input ending early (blank
read) or running long (a symbol where `w₀` is exhausted) — it switches to an
emission chain for `v`, and after matching all of `w₀` and then reading the boundary
blank it switches to an emission chain for `u` (at most `|u| + |v| + 2` further
states, one emitted symbol per step). Every run halts within
`|w₀| + max |u| |v| + 3` steps — a constant, absorbed as `c * (n + 1)`. -/
theorem computesFunInTime_ifEq (w₀ u v : List Bool) :
    ∃ (M : FinTM Bool) (c : ℕ),
      M.ComputesFunInTime (fun w => if w = w₀ then u else v) fun n => c * (n + 1) := by
  refine ⟨ifEqTM w₀ u v, w₀.length + max u.length v.length + 3, fun x => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨t, ht, hs, ho⟩ := ifEq_run w₀ u v x w₀.length 0 (by omega) (by omega) rfl
    ((ifEqTM w₀ u v).tm.initCfg x) rfl (by simp) rfl
  have hbase : (ifEqTM w₀ u v).ComputesInTime x (if x = w₀ then u else v) t :=
    ⟨_, hs, ho, rfl⟩
  exact hbase.mono (Nat.le_trans (by omega) (Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (by omega)))

/-- **Timed partial composition.** If `M₁` halts on `x` with output `y` within `t₁`
steps and `M₂` halts on `y` with output `o` within `t₂` steps, then
`bufferedCompTM M₁ M₂` halts on `x` with output `o` within `t₁ + |y| + 2 + t₂` steps.
No totality is assumed of either machine (cf. `computesFunInTime_comp`, which
requires it).

**Proof sketch.** `Turing.FinTM.bufferedComp_start` reaches the second phase, with
`M₂`'s initial configuration on virtual input `y`, within `t₁ + |y| + 2` steps;
`Turing.FinTM.bufferedSecondCfg_run` then tracks `M₂`'s run step for step, and the
embedding preserves halting and output. -/
theorem bufferedCompTM_computesInTime (M₁ M₂ : FinTM Bool) {x y o : List Bool} {t₁ t₂ : ℕ}
    (h₁ : M₁.ComputesInTime x y t₁) (h₂ : M₂.ComputesInTime y o t₂) :
    (bufferedCompTM M₁ M₂).ComputesInTime x o (t₁ + y.length + 2 + t₂) := by
  obtain ⟨a, p, tapes, heads, ha, hstart⟩ := bufferedComp_start M₁ M₂ x y t₁ h₁
  obtain ⟨b, _, hr⟩ := bufferedSecondCfg_run M₁ M₂ (M₂.tm.initCfg y) true
    (by simp [VirtualTag, MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init]) p tapes heads t₂
  have hc := (computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mp h₂
  have hbase : (bufferedCompTM M₁ M₂).ComputesInTime x o (a + t₂) := by
    apply (computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mpr
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, hstart, hr]
    exact ⟨by simpa only [bufferedSecondCfg, Option.map_eq_none_iff] using hc.1, hc.2⟩
  exact hbase.mono (by omega)

/-- **The buffered composition computes the composite**. If `M₁` computes `f` within `T₁` and `M₂`
computes `g` within a monotone `T₂`, then `bufferedCompTM M₁ M₂` computes `g ∘ f` within
`2·(T₁ n + T₂ (T₁ n) + 1)` steps. [AB09, §1.2; the composition that [AB09] leaves to high-level
descriptions.]

**Proof sketch.** `bufferedCompTM_computesInTime` gives `T₁ |x| + |f x| + 2 + T₂ |f x|`; the
intermediate word is no longer than the time that produced it (`output_length_le`), and
monotonicity of `T₂` turns `T₂ |f x|` into `T₂ (T₁ |x|)`. -/
theorem bufferedCompTM_computesFunInTime {M₁ M₂ : FinTM Bool} {f g : List Bool → List Bool}
    {T₁ T₂ : ℕ → ℕ}
    (h₁ : M₁.ComputesFunInTime f T₁) (h₂ : M₂.ComputesFunInTime g T₂)
    (hT₂ : Monotone T₂) :
    (bufferedCompTM M₁ M₂).ComputesFunInTime (g ∘ f) fun n => 2 * (T₁ n + T₂ (T₁ n) + 1) := by
  intro x
  have hlen : (f x).length ≤ T₁ x.length := by
    have ho := ((computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mp (h₁ x)).2
    simpa only [ho] using M₁.tm.output_length_le x (T₁ x.length)
  have htime : T₂ (f x).length ≤ T₂ (T₁ x.length) := hT₂ hlen
  exact (bufferedCompTM_computesInTime M₁ M₂ (h₁ x) (h₂ (f x))).mono
    (by dsimp only; omega)

/-- **Composition.** If `f` is computable within `T₁` and `g` within a monotone `T₂`,
then `g ∘ f` is computable within `c · (T₁ n + T₂ (T₁ n) + 1)`.

The inner bound `T₂ (T₁ n)` is valid because the intermediate string is no longer than
the time that produced it: `|f x| ≤ T₁ |x|` by `Turing.MultiTapeTM.output_length_le`.
Monotonicity of `T₂` is genuinely needed to convert that length bound into a time
bound.

**Proof sketch.** Build `M` with `M₁.k + M₂.k + 1` work tapes over `Bool`. Phase one
simulates `M₁` step for step on the true input, with `M₁`'s emissions written instead
onto the dedicated intermediate tape (constant overhead per step; this is the
append-only-output buffering discussed in the module docstring). Phase two rewinds the
intermediate tape head (at most `T₁ n` steps) and simulates `M₂` step for step, with
`M₂`'s input-head reads served from the intermediate tape and `M₂`'s emissions going to
the real output tape. Phase two costs constant overhead per step of `M₂`, which halts
within `T₂ |f x| ≤ T₂ (T₁ n)` steps. Bookkeeping (phase switching, boundary detection
on the intermediate tape) is absorbed into `c`.

**Implementation note (epoch 2).** The shared `bufferedCompTM` has
`M₁.k + (1 + M₂.k)` tapes and uses one physical step per simulated step.
The first halting time is at most `T₁ |x|`; rewind and dispatch take exactly
`|f x| + 2` steps, including the unconditional first left move. Consequently
`2 * T₁ |x| + T₂ (T₁ |x|) + 2` suffices, and the theorem uses `c = 2`. -/
theorem computesFunInTime_comp {M₁ M₂ : FinTM Bool} {f g : List Bool → List Bool}
    {T₁ T₂ : ℕ → ℕ}
    (h₁ : M₁.ComputesFunInTime f T₁) (h₂ : M₂.ComputesFunInTime g T₂)
    (hT₂ : Monotone T₂) :
    ∃ (M : FinTM Bool) (c : ℕ),
      M.ComputesFunInTime (g ∘ f) fun n => c * (T₁ n + T₂ (T₁ n) + 1) := by
  refine ⟨bufferedCompTM M₁ M₂, 2, fun x => ?_⟩
  have hlen : (f x).length ≤ T₁ x.length := by
    have ho := ((computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mp (h₁ x)).2
    simpa only [ho] using M₁.tm.output_length_le x (T₁ x.length)
  -- This is the only use of monotonicity: transfer the intermediate length bound.
  have htime : T₂ (f x).length ≤ T₂ (T₁ x.length) := hT₂ hlen
  exact (bufferedCompTM_computesInTime M₁ M₂ (h₁ x) (h₂ (f x))).mono
    (by dsimp only; omega)

/-- **The buffered composition on the first machine's image**. If `M` computes `f` within `T₁` and,
for every input `x`, `U` maps `f x` to `g x` within `T₂ |x|` steps, then `bufferedCompTM M U`
computes `g` within `2·T₁ n + T₂ n + 2` steps. No totality of `U` and no monotonicity is assumed.

**Proof sketch.** As `bufferedCompTM_computesFunInTime`, with the second phase's budget
measured at the original input length. -/
theorem bufferedCompTM_computesFunInTime_on_image (M U : FinTM Bool)
    (f g : List Bool → List Bool) (T₁ T₂ : ℕ → ℕ) (hM : M.ComputesFunInTime f T₁)
    (hU : ∀ x, U.ComputesInTime (f x) (g x) (T₂ x.length)) :
    (bufferedCompTM M U).ComputesFunInTime g (fun n => 2 * T₁ n + T₂ n + 2) := by
  intro x
  have hlen : (f x).length ≤ T₁ x.length := by
    have ho := ((computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mp (hM x)).2
    simpa only [ho] using M.tm.output_length_le x (T₁ x.length)
  exact (bufferedCompTM_computesInTime M U (hM x) (hU x)).mono (by dsimp only; omega)

/-- **Composition with a second machine correct only on the image.** If `M` computes `f`
within `T₁` and, for every input `x`, `U` maps `f x` to `g x` within `T₂ |x|` steps (the
budget measured at the *original* input length), then some machine computes `g` within
`2 T₁ n + T₂ n + 2`. Unlike `computesFunInTime_comp`, `U` need not be total, and no
monotonicity is assumed.

**Proof sketch.** `bufferedCompTM M U` runs both phases
(`bufferedCompTM_computesInTime`); the intermediate output is no longer than `M`'s
running time, so capture and rewind cost at most `T₁ n + 2` more steps. -/
theorem exists_comp_on_image (M U : FinTM Bool) (f g : List Bool → List Bool)
    (T₁ T₂ : ℕ → ℕ) (hM : M.ComputesFunInTime f T₁)
    (hU : ∀ x, U.ComputesInTime (f x) (g x) (T₂ x.length)) :
    ∃ N : FinTM Bool, N.ComputesFunInTime g (fun n => 2 * T₁ n + T₂ n + 2) := by
  refine ⟨bufferedCompTM M U, fun x => ?_⟩
  have hlen : (f x).length ≤ T₁ x.length := by
    have ho := ((computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mp (hM x)).2
    simpa only [ho] using M.tm.output_length_le x (T₁ x.length)
  exact (bufferedCompTM_computesInTime M U (hM x) (hU x)).mono (by dsimp only; omega)

/-- **The buffered composition's halting relation**. For all machines `M₁`, `M₂` and words `x`, `w`:
the buffered composition halts on `x` with output `w` if and only if `M₁` halts on `x` with some
output `y` and `M₂` halts on `y` with output `w`. No totality or time hypotheses.

**Proof sketch.** The body of today's `exists_comp_partial`: a divergent first phase keeps every
composite configuration live (`bufferedFirstCfg_run`); otherwise `bufferedComp_start` reaches the
second phase with `M₂`'s initial configuration on the virtual input `y`, and `bufferedSecondCfg_run`
tracks `M₂` step for step in both directions. -/
theorem bufferedCompTM_computes_iff (M₁ M₂ : FinTM Bool) (x w : List Bool) :
    (∃ t, (bufferedCompTM M₁ M₂).ComputesInTime x w t) ↔
      ∃ y : List Bool, (∃ t, M₁.ComputesInTime x y t) ∧ ∃ t, M₂.ComputesInTime y w t := by
  classical
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨t, ht⟩
    -- A divergent first component would keep every composite configuration live.
    have hh : ∃ s, (M₁.tm.runFrom (M₁.tm.initCfg x) s).state = none := by
      by_contra h
      have hr := bufferedFirstCfg_run M₁ M₂ (M₁.tm.initCfg x) t
        (fun s _ hs => h ⟨s, hs⟩)
      rw [← bufferedFirstCfg_init] at hr
      have hc := ((computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mp ht).1
      rw [hr] at hc
      simp only [bufferedFirstCfg, Option.some_ne_none] at hc
    obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := hh
    let y := (M₁.tm.runFrom (M₁.tm.initCfg x) s).output
    have hy : M₁.ComputesInTime x y s := (computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mpr ⟨hs, rfl⟩
    obtain ⟨a, p, tapes, heads, _, ha⟩ := bufferedComp_start M₁ M₂ x y s hy
    -- Extend a completed run past the verified administrative prefix.
    have hc := (computesInTime_iff _ x w (a + t)).mp (ht.mono (by omega))
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, ha] at hc
    obtain ⟨b, _, hr⟩ := bufferedSecondCfg_run M₁ M₂ (M₂.tm.initCfg y) true
      (by simp [VirtualTag, MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init]) p tapes heads t
    rw [hr] at hc
    refine ⟨y, ⟨s, hy⟩, t, (computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mpr ?_⟩
    exact ⟨by simpa only [bufferedSecondCfg, Option.map_eq_none_iff] using hc.1, hc.2⟩
  · rintro ⟨y, ⟨s, hs⟩, ⟨t, ht⟩⟩
    obtain ⟨a, p, tapes, heads, _, ha⟩ := bufferedComp_start M₁ M₂ x y s hs
    obtain ⟨b, _, hr⟩ := bufferedSecondCfg_run M₁ M₂ (M₂.tm.initCfg y) true
      (by simp [VirtualTag, MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init]) p tapes heads t
    have hc := (computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mp ht
    refine ⟨a + t, (computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mpr ?_⟩
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, ha, hr]
    exact ⟨by simpa only [bufferedSecondCfg, Option.map_eq_none_iff] using hc.1, hc.2⟩

/-- **Partial (guarded) sequential composition** — the phase-4 API obligation
identified by the phase-3 audit (round 2, finding 10 and Argument F):
`Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_comp` requires both components to compute *total*
functions, so it cannot take a partially computing machine — such as the universal
evaluator — as a component. This lemma composes two arbitrary machines at the level
of their halting relations, with **no totality or time hypotheses**: `M` behaves on
`x` exactly as `M₂` behaves on `M₁`'s completed output — halting, completed outputs,
and divergence all correspond.

Statement notes. The intermediate string `y` is existentially quantified, but by
`Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.output_unique` at most one `y` satisfies the first
conjunct, so the right-hand side reads "`M₁` halts on `x` (necessarily with a unique
`y`), and then `M₂` halts on `y` with `w`". If `M₁` diverges on `x`, or halts but
`M₂` diverges on its output, both sides are empty — `M` diverges. A time-bounded
refinement is deliberately not stated; it will be added if and when a result needs
it.

**Proof sketch** (buffered intermediate output, per the audit's design). `M` carries
`M₁`'s and `M₂`'s work tapes plus a fresh *buffer* tape. Phase one simulates `M₁` on
the true input step for step, with each emission of `M₁` written to the buffer tape
(write, move right) instead of the output tape; the append-only output discipline
makes the buffer region a verbatim copy of `M₁`'s output, contiguous from the
initial head cell. If `M₁` never halts, neither does `M`. On `M₁`'s halting
transition, `M` rewinds the buffer head to the leftmost written cell — the head
rests on the blank immediately *right* of the written word, so the rewind's first
left move is unconditional (testing the current cell before moving would stop at the
wrong end; phase-4 audit, finding 3), then left while reading a symbol, then one
step right. Phase two simulates `M₂` with its *input-tape
reads served from the buffer*: the buffer holds exactly `y` with blank cells on both
sides, and `M` maintains `M₂`'s virtual input position on it, mirroring the clamped
input-head semantics of `Turing.moveInputPos` at both boundaries — the same
virtual-boundary emulation as the universal machine's sketch
(`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Universal`); a blank read identifies a boundary,
and *which* boundary is determined by the direction of arrival, tracked in the
state — for an empty intermediate word the simulation starts with the right-boundary
tag already set, the left boundary one inward move away (phase-4 audit, finding 3).
`M₂`'s work-tape actions go to its own fresh tapes and its emissions to the
real output tape, untouched during phase one. `M` halts exactly when the simulated
`M₂` halts; step-for-step run correspondence in each phase gives both directions of
the iff.

**Implementation note (epoch 2).** The buffer and virtual-input invariants are
public in `Simulation.lean`. The arrival tag is constrained only at boundaries;
stationary moves preserve it, including suppressed outward moves. Dispatch always
sets it to true, which is already the right-boundary tag when the word is empty.
A simulated phase-one halt remains live through the exact `|y| + 2` rewind.
For the forward implication, phase-one divergence contradicts a completed run;
otherwise extend that completed run beyond the verified phase-two start using
absorbing halting, and recover the second completed computation by lockstep. -/
theorem exists_comp_partial (M₁ M₂ : FinTM Bool) :
    ∃ M : FinTM Bool, ∀ x w : List Bool,
      (∃ t, M.ComputesInTime x w t) ↔
        ∃ y : List Bool,
          (∃ t, M₁.ComputesInTime x y t) ∧ ∃ t, M₂.ComputesInTime y w t := by
  classical
  refine ⟨bufferedCompTM M₁ M₂, fun x w => ?_⟩
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨t, ht⟩
    -- A divergent first component would keep every composite configuration live.
    have hh : ∃ s, (M₁.tm.runFrom (M₁.tm.initCfg x) s).state = none := by
      by_contra h
      have hr := bufferedFirstCfg_run M₁ M₂ (M₁.tm.initCfg x) t
        (fun s _ hs => h ⟨s, hs⟩)
      rw [← bufferedFirstCfg_init] at hr
      have hc := ((computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mp ht).1
      rw [hr] at hc
      simp only [bufferedFirstCfg, Option.some_ne_none] at hc
    obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := hh
    let y := (M₁.tm.runFrom (M₁.tm.initCfg x) s).output
    have hy : M₁.ComputesInTime x y s := (computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mpr ⟨hs, rfl⟩
    obtain ⟨a, p, tapes, heads, _, ha⟩ := bufferedComp_start M₁ M₂ x y s hy
    -- Extend a completed run past the verified administrative prefix.
    have hc := (computesInTime_iff _ x w (a + t)).mp (ht.mono (by omega))
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, ha] at hc
    obtain ⟨b, _, hr⟩ := bufferedSecondCfg_run M₁ M₂ (M₂.tm.initCfg y) true
      (by simp [VirtualTag, MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init]) p tapes heads t
    rw [hr] at hc
    refine ⟨y, ⟨s, hy⟩, t, (computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mpr ?_⟩
    exact ⟨by simpa only [bufferedSecondCfg, Option.map_eq_none_iff] using hc.1, hc.2⟩
  · rintro ⟨y, ⟨s, hs⟩, ⟨t, ht⟩⟩
    obtain ⟨a, p, tapes, heads, _, ha⟩ := bufferedComp_start M₁ M₂ x y s hs
    obtain ⟨b, _, hr⟩ := bufferedSecondCfg_run M₁ M₂ (M₂.tm.initCfg y) true
      (by simp [VirtualTag, MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init]) p tapes heads t
    have hc := (computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mp ht
    refine ⟨a + t, (computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mpr ?_⟩
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, ha, hr]
    exact ⟨by simpa only [bufferedSecondCfg, Option.map_eq_none_iff] using hc.1, hc.2⟩

/-- **The untimed conditional**. Run `D` with its first emission captured in a state register,
rewind the input, then enter `M₁` or `M₂` on disjoint fresh tapes according to the register; an
empty register at dispatch halts. -/
def condTM (D M₁ M₂ : FinTM Bool) : FinTM Bool where
  k := D.k + (M₁.k + M₂.k)
  State := (Option D.State × Option Bool) ⊕ (Option Bool ⊕ (M₁.State ⊕ M₂.State))
  tm :=
    { q₀ := .inl (some D.tm.q₀, none)
      tr := fun q inp work => match q with
        | .inl (some q, reg) =>
          let a := D.tm.tr q inp (fun i => work (Fin.castAdd (M₁.k + M₂.k) i))
          ⟨a.inputTape, Fin.addCases a.workTapes (fun _ => (none, 0)), none,
            some (.inl (a.state, reg.or a.output))⟩
        | .inl (none, reg) => controlAction .neg (some (.inr (.inl reg)))
        | .inr (.inl reg) => match inp with
          | some _ => controlAction .neg (some (.inr (.inl reg)))
          | none => controlAction .pos
              (reg.map (fun b => .inr (.inr (branchTM M₁ M₂ b).tm.q₀)))
        | .inr (.inr q) => rightAction D.k (fun s => .inr (.inr s))
            ((branchTM M₁ M₂ false).tm.tr q inp (fun i => work (Fin.natAdd D.k i))) }

/-- Embed a controller configuration with its output suppressed and the first
output symbol stored in the finite register. All branch tapes remain blank. -/
private def controlCfg (D M₁ M₂ : FinTM Bool) {x : List Bool}
    (c : Cfg D.k Bool D.State x) : Cfg (condTM D M₁ M₂).k Bool (condTM D M₁ M₂).State x where
  state := some (.inl (c.state, c.output.head?))
  inputPos := c.inputPos
  workTapes := Fin.addCases c.workTapes (fun _ _ => none)
  workTapePos := Fin.addCases c.workTapePos (fun _ => 0)
  output := []

/-- Before the simulated controller halts, one composite step exactly updates its
configuration and the first-emission register. The head-of-append identity makes
this invariant valid even without any assumption on the controller's output. -/
private lemma controlCfg_step (D M₁ M₂ : FinTM Bool) {x : List Bool}
    (c : Cfg D.k Bool D.State x) (hs : c.state ≠ none) :
    (condTM D M₁ M₂).tm.step (controlCfg D M₁ M₂ c) =
      controlCfg D M₁ M₂ (D.tm.step c) := by
  unfold MultiTapeTM.step
  cases hq : c.state with
  | none => exact False.elim (hs hq)
  | some q =>
    have hs' : (controlCfg D M₁ M₂ c).state = some (.inl (some q, c.output.head?)) := by
      simp [controlCfg, hq]
    rw [hs']
    dsimp only [condTM]
    have hr : (fun i => (controlCfg D M₁ M₂ c).workTapeSymbols
        (Fin.castAdd (M₁.k + M₂.k) i)) = c.workTapeSymbols := by
      funext i
      simp [controlCfg, Cfg.workTapeSymbols]
    have hi : (controlCfg D M₁ M₂ c).inputSymbol = c.inputSymbol := rfl
    rw [hr, hi]
    refine Cfg.ext ?_ rfl ?_ ?_ ?_
    · simp [controlCfg, Action.apply, List.head?_append, Option.head?_toList]
    · funext i
      refine Fin.addCases ?_ ?_ i <;> intro j <;> simp [controlCfg, Action.apply]
    · funext i
      refine Fin.addCases ?_ ?_ i <;> intro j <;> simp [controlCfg, Action.apply]
    · simp [controlCfg, Action.apply]

/-- Controller lockstep holds through its first halting step. Subsequent composite
steps perform the rewind, so no claim of lockstep after halting is made. -/
private lemma controlCfg_run (D M₁ M₂ : FinTM Bool) {x : List Bool}
    (c : Cfg D.k Bool D.State x) (t : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ s, s < t → (D.tm.runFrom c s).state ≠ none) :
    (condTM D M₁ M₂).tm.runFrom (controlCfg D M₁ M₂ c) t =
      controlCfg D M₁ M₂ (D.tm.runFrom c t) := by
  induction t with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ t ih =>
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', ih (fun s hs => h s (by omega)),
      controlCfg_step D M₁ M₂ _ (h t (by omega)), MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step']

/-- A completed singleton controller computation reaches the selected branch's
fresh initial configuration after a finite prefix.

**Proof sketch.** Choose the first halting time of `D` and use controller lockstep.
Output uniqueness identifies its completed output with `[b]`, so the register is
`some b`, including when that bit was emitted early. Rewind from the resulting
input position; the branch tapes and real output have remained untouched. -/
private lemma condTM_start (D M₁ M₂ : FinTM Bool) (x : List Bool) (b : Bool)
    (hD : ∃ t, D.ComputesInTime x [b] t) :
    ∃ (t : ℕ) (tapes : Fin D.k → ℤ → Option Bool) (heads : Fin D.k → ℤ),
      (condTM D M₁ M₂).tm.runFrom ((condTM D M₁ M₂).tm.initCfg x) t =
        rightCfg (fun q => .inr (.inr q)) ((branchTM M₁ M₂ b).tm.initCfg x) tapes heads := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨tD, hDc⟩ := hD
  have hh : ∃ t, (D.tm.runFrom (D.tm.initCfg x) t).state = none :=
    ⟨tD, ((computesInTime_iff D x [b] tD).mp hDc).1⟩
  let t := Nat.find hh
  let cf := D.tm.runFrom (D.tm.initCfg x) t
  have hstop : cf.state = none := Nat.find_spec hh
  have hc : D.ComputesInTime x cf.output t :=
    (computesInTime_iff D x cf.output t).mpr ⟨hstop, rfl⟩
  have hout : cf.output = [b] := hc.output_unique hDc
  have hi : (condTM D M₁ M₂).tm.initCfg x = controlCfg D M₁ M₂ (D.tm.initCfg x) := by
    refine Cfg.ext rfl rfl ?_ ?_ rfl
    · funext i
      refine Fin.addCases ?_ ?_ i <;> intro j <;> simp [controlCfg]
    · funext i
      refine Fin.addCases ?_ ?_ i <;> intro j <;> simp [controlCfg]
  have hrun : (condTM D M₁ M₂).tm.runFrom ((condTM D M₁ M₂).tm.initCfg x) t =
      controlCfg D M₁ M₂ cf := by
    rw [hi]
    exact controlCfg_run D M₁ M₂ (D.tm.initCfg x) t (fun s hs => Nat.find_min hh hs)
  obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := rewind_from_any (condTM D M₁ M₂).tm
    (.inl (none, some b)) (.inr (.inl (some b)))
    (some (.inr (.inr (branchTM M₁ M₂ b).tm.q₀)))
    (fun _ _ => rfl) (fun inp _ => by cases inp <;> rfl)
    (controlCfg D M₁ M₂ cf) (by simp [controlCfg, hstop, hout])
  refine ⟨t + r, cf.workTapes, cf.workTapePos, ?_⟩
  rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, hrun, hr]
  rfl

/-- **The untimed conditional's halting relation**. If `D` computes `x ↦ [p x]`, then on every input
`x` the conditional halts with output `w` if and only if the branch `cond (p x) M₁ M₂` halts on `x`
with output `w`.

**Proof sketch.** The body of today's `exists_cond`: the private `condTM_start` reaches the selected
branch's initial configuration, after which `rightCfg_run` tracks the branch union step for step and
`branchTM_computes` identifies the selected branch. -/
theorem condTM_computes_iff (D M₁ M₂ : FinTM Bool) (p : List Bool → Bool)
    (hD : D.Computes fun x => [p x]) (x w : List Bool) :
    (∃ t, (condTM D M₁ M₂).ComputesInTime x w t) ↔
      ∃ t, (cond (p x) M₁ M₂).ComputesInTime x w t := by
  sorry

/-- **Branching on a decided predicate** — the second phase-4 combinator (phase-3
audit, round 2, Argument F, step 2 of the `HALT → UC` reduction): given a total
decider `D` for `p` and two branch machines, some machine behaves on every input
exactly as the branch selected by `p` does *on that same input*. The input tape is
read-only, so both branches see the original input.

**Proof sketch.** `D` computes the singleton output `[p x]` on every input, and
output is append-only, so along any run `D` emits exactly one symbol; simulate `D`
with that single emission recorded in a state register instead of emitted (no buffer
tape needed). On `D`'s halting transition, rewind the true input head to its initial
position: one step left, then left while reading a symbol, then one step right —
from any position this ends at input position `1`, the initial position, the clamp
at position `0` making the walk safe (including on empty input). Then transfer
control to a disjoint copy of `M₁` or `M₂` according to the register. The branches'
work tapes are fresh tapes `D` never touched, the output tape is untouched by phase
one, and the input head is back at its initial position, so the selected branch's
run is reproduced verbatim; determinism (`Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.output_unique`)
identifies `D`'s completed output with `[p x]`, so the selected branch is
`cond (p x) M₁ M₂`.

The implementation retains the first emission, with the exact invariant that the
register is the head of the simulated output. A live administrative state follows
the simulated halt before the first left move. For the forward implication, extend
any completed composite run beyond the verified branch-start prefix using absorbing
halting, then apply branch lockstep; the reverse implication concatenates that
prefix with the selected branch run. -/
theorem exists_cond (D M₁ M₂ : FinTM Bool) (p : List Bool → Bool)
    (hD : D.Computes fun x => [p x]) :
    ∃ M : FinTM Bool, ∀ x w : List Bool,
      (∃ t, M.ComputesInTime x w t) ↔
        ∃ t, (cond (p x) M₁ M₂).ComputesInTime x w t := by
  refine ⟨condTM D M₁ M₂, fun x w => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨a, tapes, heads, ha⟩ := condTM_start D M₁ M₂ x (p x) (hD x)
  have hr (t : ℕ) :
      (condTM D M₁ M₂).tm.runFrom ((condTM D M₁ M₂).tm.initCfg x) (a + t) =
        rightCfg (fun q => .inr (.inr q))
          ((branchTM M₁ M₂ (p x)).tm.runFrom ((branchTM M₁ M₂ (p x)).tm.initCfg x) t)
          tapes heads := by
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, ha]
    exact rightCfg_run (branchTM M₁ M₂ (p x)).tm (condTM D M₁ M₂).tm
      (fun q => .inr (.inr q)) (fun _ _ _ => rfl) _ tapes heads t
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨t, ht⟩
    have hc := (computesInTime_iff (condTM D M₁ M₂) x w (a + t)).mp
      (ht.mono (by omega))
    rw [hr t] at hc
    have hb : (branchTM M₁ M₂ (p x)).ComputesInTime x w t :=
      (computesInTime_iff _ x w t).mpr
        ⟨by simpa only [rightCfg, Option.map_eq_none_iff] using hc.1, hc.2⟩
    exact ⟨t, (branchTM_computes M₁ M₂ (p x) x w t).mp hb⟩
  · rintro ⟨t, ht⟩
    have hb := (computesInTime_iff (branchTM M₁ M₂ (p x)) x w t).mp
      ((branchTM_computes M₁ M₂ (p x) x w t).mpr ht)
    refine ⟨a + t, (computesInTime_iff _ x w (a + t)).mpr ?_⟩
    rw [hr t]
    exact ⟨by simpa only [rightCfg, Option.map_eq_none_iff] using hb.1, hb.2⟩

end Turing.FinTM
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Simulation.lean =====

```
/-
